# R2 go/no-go — two-index K=3 sector T_ij = κ[h_i,h_i,h_j] (pre-registered 2026-09-26)

Status: **criterion written BEFORE the experiment ran.** Results are appended below the line at the end;
nothing above the line was edited after the run.

## What R2 claims (ALGORITHM_SPEC.md §R2)
1. Linear step: κ[z_i,z_i,z_j] = Σ_ab W_ai² W_bj T_ab + 2 Σ_{a≠a'} W_ai W_a'i W_bj κ[h_a,h_a',h_b]; first term
   exact from the two-index sector, second (distinct-index) term at leading Hermite order (path diagram).
   Diagonal κ₃(z_i) = 3 Σ_ac W_ai² W_ci T_ac − 2 Σ_a W_ai³ T_aa + distinct.
2. ReLU step: T for the outputs from the trivariate Hermite formula to ALL orders in C_ij, i.e.
   κ[φ_i,φ_i,φ_j] = Cov(φ_i²,φ_j) − 2 m1_i Cov(φ_i,φ_j) with Cov(f_i,g_j) = Σ_k f̂_k ĝ_k C_ij^k / k!,
   plus first-order Gram–Charlier terms from the incoming two-index sector of z.
3. Feedback of κ[z_i,z_i,z_j] into Σ, and the Edgeworth κ₃/6 readout correction.

## Numbers the criterion is derived from (spec F2/F3, N=1e6, 2 MLPs)
- Per-step closure error with MC-exact (μ,Σ) of layer 15 (Gaussian readout): **1.64e-7 / 1.77e-7**.
- Same readout with the MC-exact κ₃(z₁₆) Edgeworth term: **2.1e-8 / 2.1e-8** → κ₃ carries **~87 %** of a
  step's error. That is the CEILING for anything κ₃-based: exact κ₃ would give ≈ 8× per step, and with
  ~16 near-additive steps ≈ 8× on the final MSE (3.6e-6 → ~4e-7 uncalibrated). **60× (the leader gap) is
  therefore NOT reachable from κ₃ alone**; R2 can at best close about half of the log-gap, and the rest
  needs κ₄. The spec's "10–60×" is an upper bound that already assumes κ₄ follows.
- K3-lite (leading diagrams) recovers 1/3.8 of the κ₃ amplitude (slope MC/est 3.76 / 3.85) and buys
  −14…−19 % final MSE. Any R2 verdict must clearly beat that.

## Pre-stated criterion
Oracle protocol: ONE closure step from MC-exact statistics of layer 15 (post-ReLU h₁₅ and/or
pre-activation z₁₅), all references N ≥ 1e6, 2 MLPs (seeds 1000, 1001 — the same MLPs as the spec).

**GO** iff BOTH hold on BOTH MLPs:
- **(G1, mechanism)** the R2 linear step fed the MC-exact T of h₁₅ predicts the diagonal κ₃(z₁₆) with
  regression slope MC/pred in **[0.7, 1.4]** and residual mean-square ≤ **50 %** of the MC κ₃ mean-square
  (K3-lite: slope 3.8, residual 92 %). This tests whether the two-index sector CARRIES most of κ₃(z).
- **(G2, payoff)** the FULL R2 chain from MC-exact (μ, Σ, T) of z₁₅ (ReLU closure → T_h → linear step →
  κ₃(z₁₆) → Edgeworth readout) removes **≥ 60 %** of the κ₃-attributable per-step closure error, measured
  noise-free as `1 − MSE(readout_R2 − readout_exactκ₃) / MSE(readout_Gauss − readout_exactκ₃)`.
  Justification for X = 60 %: the ceiling is 100 % of the κ₃ part (= 87 % of the step); 60 % of it ≈ 2.5×
  per step ≈ 2.5× on the final MSE uncalibrated (≈ 1.4e-6 → with per-layer calibration plausibly
  ~4–5e-7 → adjusted ~4.5e-8), i.e. R2 would deliver ≥ 2/3 of everything a κ₃ mechanism can, and only then
  is the κ₄ follow-on (the real leader-tier lever) worth building on top of it. Below 60 % the two-index
  truncation is losing more than the exact-κ₃ ceiling allows and κ₄ on the same truncation would inherit
  the loss.
- Secondary (reported, not gating): slope/residual of the ReLU step alone (T_h from exact z₁₅ stats vs MC
  T_h), of the off-diagonal two-index sector T_z16, of the Σ-feedback on Σ_h15, and the FLOP cost.

**NO-GO** otherwise. Differences below the stated reference noise are not claimed.

MC noise statements to be reported alongside: κ₃ per-neuron noise var ≈ 6σ⁶/N; T_ab noise from the
accumulated E[h_a⁴h_b²]; readout MSE noise ~σ²_final/N ≈ 7e-8 (hence the noise-free differential above).

## Results (appended after the run)
Run 2026-09-26/27, `proto_r2.py` (one-step oracle), `proto_r2_e2e.py` (16-layer closure), `proto_r2_diag.py`;
raw output in `proto_r2_results.txt`, `proto_r2_e2e_results.txt`, `proto_r2_diag_results.txt`. N=1e6, MLPs 1000/1001,
MC seeds 99/100 (same as the spec). MC refs cached in `mc_cache_mlp{0,1}_N1000000.npz`.

Deviation from the pre-registered METHODS text (criterion untouched): the T noise was measured from two independent MC seeds (N=2e4, scaled 1/N) instead of the accumulated E[h_a⁴h_b²] formula, which is wrong here — μ_h² ≈ 0.93 ≫ var_h ≈ 0.078 and the cumulant estimator cancels the mean-driven fluctuation (formula gave 972 % 'noise' while a prediction matched T to 0.4 %).

**Reference noise (measured, two independent seeds):** κ₃(z₁₆) per neuron 0.04 % of signal; T_h15 0.08 %; T_z16 0.10 %;
final-MSE noise 7.2e-8 (differences < 2e-7 between estimators vs MC are NOT resolvable; estimator-vs-estimator
differences and Test-C fractions are noise-free differentials on the same samples).

### Pre-stated gates — both PASS on both MLPs
| gate | MLP 0 | MLP 1 | threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 slope MC/pred of κ₃(z₁₆) from exact T_h15 (two-equal exact + path) | 0.994 (corr 0.976, resid 4.7 %) | 0.993 (corr 0.976, resid 4.8 %) | [0.7,1.4], resid ≤ 50 % |
| G1 reference: K3-lite same protocol | 4.75, resid 88 % | 4.43, resid 87 % | |
| G2 full chain from z₁₅ (μ,Σ,T) → readout, κ₃-attributable step error removed | **72.7 %** | **76.3 %** | ≥ 60 % |
| G2 references: oracle-T 76.4 / 78.5 %; K3-lite 16.2 / 12.2 %; chain WITHOUT the GC input-κ₃ terms 17.9 / 13.4 % | | | |

Mechanism facts: (a) the ReLU step generates almost no new two-index κ₃ — all-order Hermite with Gaussian inputs
leaves T_h15 resid 0.61/0.57 (≈ K3-lite 0.63), while the first-order Gram–Charlier terms in the INCOMING sector
give resid 0.002/0.003 and Σ_h15 off-diag MSE 1.4e-9 (kit 4.1e-7, noise 7e-9). The sector is inherited, not
generated; "all Hermite orders" buys nothing measurable. (b) The distinct-index 3-tensor contributes 6 % of
κ₃(z₁₆) m.s. per step but 17–18 % of the off-diagonal T_z16 m.s.; the leading-order path diagram recovers only
20 % of it (resid 0.81), and its off-diagonal form without coincident-index exclusions OVER-corrects.
(c) Bug found and fixed on the way: the spec's second sum contains exact two-index terms (b∈{a,a'}:
`2Σ_{a≠a'} W_ai W_aj W_a'i T_aa'`, one extra matmul); dropping them under-propagates the diagonal 3× (first
e2e run showed a spurious 4.2× deficit).

### End-to-end (16 layers, ZERO shipped constants) — not pre-registered, added after the smoke test
| estimator | MLP 0 | MLP 1 | rel. scale (bias) |
|---|---|---|---|
| kit | 3.61e-6 | 4.92e-6 | 0.99842 / 0.99791 |
| **R2 two-index sector (no path)** | **9.71e-7** | **9.47e-7** | 0.99983 / 0.99973 |
| R2 + in-sample per-layer scale (optimistic) | 9.43e-7 | 8.87e-7 | |
| R1 = k3lite + shipped per-layer cal (spec, 6 train MLPs) | 1.07e-6 | 1.12e-6 | |
| R2 + off-diag path term | 1.53e-6 | 1.46e-6 | 1.00064 (over-corrects) |
| R2, T gain 1.02/layer | 1.03e-6 / 1.07e-6 | 0.97e-6 / 1.01e-6 | 0.9999 / 1.0000 |
R2 vs R1-cal differs by 1.0–1.7e-7 — below the 2e-7 resolution. Propagated κ₃(z₁₆) after 16 steps: slope 1.36/1.45,
corr 0.97, resid 0.13/0.16 (per-layer slope drifts 1.0 → 1.4: the missing distinct-index sector accumulates);
T_h15 resid 0.15/0.17 (53–56 % rank-1). Remaining error is per-neuron scatter, not amplitude: μ_z16 MSE 1.9/1.7e-6
(kit 7.0/8.9e-6), σ_z16 MSE 1.0e-5 (kit 1.8e-4), Σ_z16 off-diag 3.0e-6 — consistent with ~14 × the 7e-8 per-step
residual. Gains on the sector or the readout κ₃ do not help (≥3 on the readout κ₃ destabilises the GC variance).

### Cost (n=1024, per layer → ×16 / 2^41)
κ₂ symmetric einsum 3.2e9 + sector 3 matmuls (`(W∘W)ᵀT`, `T W`, `(W∘P)ᵀW`) 6.4e9 + n² Hermite/GC ≈ 5e8 → 1.0e10 →
**1.6e11 = 7.4 %** (R2 REPLACES R1's K3-lite block, whose R1 total was 7.0 %). With the path term 13.7 % — over the
floor and it hurts; drop it. Must be metered exactly with `budget_summary()`; all C-powers as `fnp.multiply` chains.

### Verdict
- **Against the pre-stated criterion: GO** (G1 and G2 met on both MLPs; K3-lite fails both by a wide margin).
- **Against the stated goal ("close most of the ~60× gap"): NO.** Measured e2e gain is 3.7–5.2× over v0 uncalibrated
  → adjusted ≈ 9.5e-8, i.e. ≈ R1-calibrated (1.05e-7) with **no data files**; leader 1.7e-9 is still ~56× away.
  κ₃-anything is capped at ~8×/step by the exact-κ₃ ceiling (spec F2); R2 reaches ~75 % of that per step.
- Recommendation: ship R2 (no path) as the zero-constant replacement for R1's calibrated K3-lite (removes the
  calibration-transfer risk, spec §3.4, at ~equal score); do NOT sell it as the leader-tier lever.
- **Next best idea (concrete):** the same two-index trick one order up — Q_ij = κ[h_i,h_i,h_j,h_j] (n²), linear step
  `(W∘W)ᵀ Q (W∘W)` + coincident-index terms (~3 matmuls, +3 % budget → ~10.4 %, multiplier penalty 4 %), ReLU step by
  first-order GC in the incoming sector (the pattern that worked for κ₃), fed into the VARIANCE (σ_z16 error is now
  the dominant residual) and the mean readout (`κ₄/24·E[f⁗]`). Go/no-go the same way: one-step oracle from MC-exact
  layer-15 (μ,Σ,T,Q) must remove ≥ 60 % of the remaining 2.1e-8/step, else the 1.5e-8 Edgeworth floor (forum 18193)
  says the leaders are not doing per-neuron cumulant readout at all and the closure family should be abandoned for
  the leader tier. Cheaper distinct-index fix for κ₃ (15–17 %/step into T): a learned per-layer gain is NOT it
  (measured above); exact-exclusion path term costs +6n³ and captures ≤ 20 % — not worth it.

# Q-sector gate — four-index K=4 sector Q_ij = κ[h_i,h_i,h_j,h_j] (pre-registered 2026-09-27 04:36 UTC)

Status: **criterion written BEFORE any Q code ran.** Results appended below the second line; nothing in this
section above that line is edited after the run.

## What the Q rung claims (on top of R2 WITHOUT the path term)
1. Linear step: κ[z_i,z_i,z_j,z_j] ⊇ Σ_ab W_ai² W_bj² Q_ab = ((W∘W)ᵀ Q (W∘W))_ij (the (a=a', b=b') pairing, exact
   from the sector, 2 matmuls). The two cross pairings (a=b, a'=b') and (a=b', a'=b) are exact n⁴ (uᵢⱼᵀ Q uᵢⱼ,
   u_ij = W_:i∘W_:j) and are only affordable through a rank-r factorisation of Q (r matmuls) — tested as a
   diagnostic at r ≤ 2, not part of the shipped step. Diagonal κ₄(z_i) = 3 Σ_ab W_ai² W_bi² Q_ab − 2 Σ_a W_ai⁴ Q_aa
   (all three pairings coincide there; exact from the sector). Patterns (3,1), (2,1,1), (1,1,1,1) are NOT tracked.
2. ReLU step: first-order Gram–Charlier in the incoming four-index sector (the pattern that worked for κ₃):
   E[f(z_a)g(z_b)] += Q_aa/24·E_G[f⁗g] + Q_bb/24·E_G[f g⁗] + Q_ab/4·E_G[f″g″]; applied to E[φφ], E[φ²φ], E[φ²φ²]
   and the per-neuron moments m1..m4 → outputs (μ, Σ, T, Q) of h. The (3,1) GC terms are dropped (untracked).
3. Readout: mean E[ReLU(z)] += κ₄/24·E_G[f⁗] = κ₄ φ(α) He₂(−α)/(24σ³); variance via the same GC in Σ.

## Numbers the criterion is derived from
- After exact κ₃ the one-step readout residual (same-sample) is **2.07e-8 / 2.12e-8** (R2 Test C); the R2 chain
  from z₁₅ stats leaves 7.0e-8 / 6.9e-8 — so the κ₃ part still left by R2 (~4.9e-8) is LARGER than the whole
  remaining post-exact-κ₃ residual. The Q rung can only address the 2.1e-8.
- e2e R2 (no path) = 9.71e-7 / 9.47e-7; R1-calibrated 1.07e-6 / 1.12e-6; leaders 1.5–1.7e-8 (adjusted 1.7e-9).
- Budget: R2 (no path) 1.6e11 = 7.4 %. The (W∘W)ᵀQ(W∘W) step is 2 matmuls = 4.3e9/layer ≈ +3.1 % naively;
  skipping the sector work at layer 1 (T=Q=0 for Gaussian input) and computing only the diagonal contractions
  at layer 16 brings R2+Q to ≈ 2.1e11 ≈ 9.5 %. Any cross-pairing matmul pushes it over 10 %.

## Pre-stated criterion
Oracle protocol as for R2: ONE step from MC-exact layer-15 statistics (μ, Σ, T, Q of z₁₅ and of h₁₅), N = 1e6,
same MLPs (1000, 1001) and the SAME sample stream as the cached refs (seeds 99/100), so all readout numbers are
same-sample differentials.

**GO** iff ALL hold on BOTH MLPs:
- **(Q1, mechanism)** κ₄(z₁₆) diagonal from the MC-exact Q_h15 through the linear step: regression slope MC/pred in
  **[0.7, 1.4]**, residual mean-square ≤ **50 %** of MC κ₄(z₁₆) m.s. Tests whether the (2,2) sector CARRIES κ₄(z).
- **(Q2, payoff)** the FULL chain from MC-exact (μ, Σ, T, Q) of z₁₅ (GC ReLU step → linear step → κ₄(z₁₆)) fed into
  the mean readout together with the MC-EXACT κ₃(z₁₆) removes **≥ 60 %** of the residual step error left after exact
  κ₃: `1 − MSE(readout[κ₃_mc, κ₄_chain] − μ_h16_mc) / MSE(readout[κ₃_mc] − μ_h16_mc)` (the 2.1e-8 → ≤ 8.4e-9).
  Reported alongside, not gating: the same fraction with exact κ₄ (the κ₄ CEILING — if even this is < 60 % the
  residual is not κ₄ and the readout-cumulant family is exhausted at this rung), and the noise-free differential
  `1 − MSE(ro[κ₄_chain] − ro[κ₄_mc]) / MSE(ro[κ₃ only] − ro[κ₄_mc])`.
- **(Q3, matters end-to-end)** the 16-layer R2+Q closure (zero constants) reaches final MSE **≤ 3.0e-7 on both MLPs**
  (≥ 3× over R2's 9.5–9.7e-7; noise floor 7.2e-8 is included in every e2e number, so 3.0e-7 is ~4× the floor and
  resolvable), at a metered cost **≤ 10 % of 2^41 including R2** (i.e. total ≤ 2.2e11 FLOP by the spec's op counts).
  Justification: at 3e-7 uncalibrated (adjusted 3e-8) the estimator would sit within 2× of the leaders; anything
  weaker than 3× is inside what the shipped per-layer calibration already buys on R2 and does not justify a
  second n² sector in the residual-time budget.
- Secondary (reported, not gating): slope/resid of Q_h15 from exact z₁₅ stats (ReLU step alone, with/without the
  Q GC terms), of the off-diagonal Q_z16 sector with and without a rank-1/2 cross-pairing term, Σ_h15 / σ_z16 MSE
  with the κ₄ feedback, FLOP count.

**NO-GO** otherwise. If NO-GO and the κ₄ ceiling itself is < 60 %, the statement to make is that the per-neuron
cumulant-readout (closure) family is exhausted at this shape and budget, and the leader tier needs a different
family. Differences below the stated reference noise are not claimed.

Reference noise to report: κ₄(z₁₆) per-neuron var ≈ 96σ⁸/N (Gaussian formula, empirical factor from two seeds);
Q_h15 / Q_z16 off-diagonal noise measured from two independent N=2e4 seeds scaled 1/N (the R2 method); readout
MSE noise 7.2e-8 (same-sample differentials only).

Also pre-registered (submission track, cheap): R2 (no path) + R1-style per-layer constants c_l refit on R2 outputs
over seeds 5000–5023 (existing 3e5-sample refs in r1_data/), evaluated on MLPs 9000/9001 (1e7 refs, noise 7e-9)
against the shipped R1-calibrated 1.25e-6 / 1.12e-6 and on MLPs 1000/1001 (1e6 refs). Expectation: within noise of
uncalibrated R2 (its per-layer scale is already 0.9998), i.e. NO material gain; reported either way.

Run 2026-09-27 04:40–05:20 UTC. `proto_q.py` (oracle, Tests A–D) → `proto_q_results.txt`; `proto_q_e2e.py` →
`proto_q_e2e_results.txt`; `fit_r2_calibration.py` → `fit_r2_calibration_results.txt`. N=1e6, MLPs 1000/1001, the SAME
sample stream as the R2 caches (asserted: recomputed μ_z identical to 1e-9), new Q refs cached in
`mc_cache_q_mlp{0,1}_N1000000.npz` (Q_z15, Q_h15, Q_z16, κ₄ per layer). Per-neuron κ₄(z₁₆) noise 0.6/0.9 % of signal
(two seeds; the Gaussian 96σ⁸/N formula overstates it 3×), Q_h15 0.8 %, Q_z16 0.9–1.1 %. Mean excess kurtosis of z₁₆
+0.066/+0.064 (κ₃: mean|skew| 0.09).

### Pre-stated gates
| gate | MLP 0 | MLP 1 | threshold | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 κ₄(z₁₆) from MC-exact Q_h15, (2,2) pairings | slope 1.005, resid 0.216 (corr 0.19) | slope 1.012, resid 0.189 (corr 0.23) | slope ∈ [0.7,1.4], resid ≤ 0.5 | **PASS** |
| Q1 reference: diag Q_aa only | slope 116, resid 0.99 | slope 105, resid 0.99 | | |
| Q2 chain from z₁₅ (μ,Σ,T,Q), readout with κ₃_mc + κ₄_chain: post-exact-κ₃ residual removed | **68.9 %** (2.07e-8 → 6.45e-9) | **75.1 %** (2.12e-8 → 5.27e-9) | ≥ 60 % | **PASS** |
| Q2 references: oracle-Q 69.0/75.3 %; chain WITHOUT the κ₄ GC input terms 30.8/27.6 %; diag-only 2 %; κ₄ CEILING (exact κ₄) **98.5 %** (→ 3.1e-10) | | | | |
| Q3 e2e 16 layers, zero constants | **9.02e-7** (R2 9.71e-7, −7 %) | **8.51e-7** (R2 9.47e-7, −10 %) | ≤ 3.0e-7 on both | **FAIL** |
| Q3 cost (spec op counts) | | | ≤ 10 % incl. R2 | 7.4 + 2.8 = **10.2 %** (2 matmuls/layer, layer 1 skipped, layer 16 diag-only) — marginal |

Untracked κ₄ patterns ((3,1),(2,1,1),(1,1,1,1)) = 19–22 % of κ₄(z₁₆) m.s.; a rank-1/2 cross-pairing term changes nothing
(resid 0.163/0.148 unchanged → do not build it). ReLU step: first-order GC in the incoming Q reproduces Q_h15 to resid
0.002 (Gaussian input: 0.92–0.95; κ₃-only: 0.58–0.61) — again inherited, not generated. Side effects of κ₄ feedback
are real and large in the ORACLE: var_h15 MSE 2.4e-8 → 2.5e-10, μ_h15 2.5e-8 → 3.5e-10, Σ_h15 off-diag 1.4e-9 → 8e-10.
Test D (one full step from z₁₅ stats, everything predicted): kit-like 3.5/3.7e-7 → R2 1.10/1.04e-7 → Q **5.56/5.07e-8**
(μ_z16 MSE 6.6e-10, σ_z16 1.1e-8). e2e: Q fixes the κ₃ slope drift (1.36/1.45 → 1.06/1.09), σ_z16 MSE 1.0e-5 → 3.5e-6,
κ₄(z₁₆) propagated slope 1.19/1.22 (drifts 1.00 → 1.2 over depth), but the final MSE moves only 5.0–5.3e-7 noise-free,
i.e. 16 × 5.3e-8 ≈ 8.5e-7 — exactly Test D's per-step floor.

### Why the payoff fails although both mechanisms pass
The remaining per-step error is not κ₄: with EXACT κ₃ the Q chain leaves 6e-9, but with the CHAIN's κ₃ it leaves 5.5e-8.
The R2 κ₃ propagation from z₁₅ stats removes only 73–76 % of the κ₃ part even with an exact T_h15 (76–78 %); the rest is
the distinct-index three-point structure κ[h_a,h_a',h_b] (a≠a'≠b) that no two-index sector carries and whose path-diagram
proxy recovers ≤ 20 % and over-corrects off-diagonal. This ~4.5e-8/step × 16 ≈ 7–9e-7 is the wall for every
index-sector truncation, κ₄ included. Adding κ₄ to the same truncation buys 2× per step in the oracle and 1.1× e2e.

### Submission track (pre-registered): R2 (no path) + per-layer constants refit on R2 (24 MLPs, 3e5 refs)
Constants are flat: 1.0000 → 0.99978 (R1's k3lite: → 0.9985). On the 1e7-ref MLPs 9000/9001 (noise 7e-9):
R1-cal 1.251e-6 / 1.119e-6; R2 uncal 1.092e-6 / 1.204e-6; **R2 × cal_r2 1.012e-6 / 1.081e-6** (mean 1.047e-6 vs R1 1.185e-6,
−12 %); the final scalar alone gives the identical number (0.99978). On 1000/1001 (1e6): 9.45e-7 / 8.89e-7 vs R1 1.04/1.18e-6.
Noise-free R2 uncal vs cal differential 3–5e-8. Real but small: ≈ 1.05e-6 → adjusted ≈ 1.1e-7 at 7.4 % budget, one 16-float
file (or one scalar). Leaders 1.5–1.7e-8 (adjusted 1.7e-9) remain ~60× away.

### Verdict: **NO-GO for the Q sector** (Q3 failed; the gate required all three)
- Mechanism is sound (Q1, Q2 pass; 2 matmuls/layer; exact κ₄ would remove 98.5 % of the post-κ₃ readout residual), so the
  per-neuron cumulant READOUT is not the limit — the exact-cumulant Edgeworth readout is essentially perfect here.
  This matches forum 18193 (thylinao: Edgeworth with true κ₃,κ₄ → 1.5–2.2e-8 vs the 1e9 truth; "dependence structure
  dominates the residual"; marginal-exact oracle 2.1e-6 vs true-cumulant readout 7.1e-7) and the leaders' 1.5–1.7e-8,
  which sit AT that exact-cumulant floor. The leaders are therefore propagating the cumulants themselves almost exactly.
- **The index-sector closure family (diag → two-index → four-index) is exhausted**: every rung inherits the distinct-index
  κ₃ loss (~4.5e-8/step, 16 steps ≈ 8e-7). Do not build (3,1) sectors, cross-pairing terms, or gains on top of it.
- **Single most promising alternative family: low-rank (CP/Tucker) propagation of the FULL third (then fourth) cumulant
  tensor instead of index truncation.** Evidence: the part of T_h15 that R2 misses is 53–56 % rank-1 and 89 % rank-32
  (proto_r2_diag); the distinct-index (1,1,1) Hermite diagram Φ_aΦ_bΦ_c κ[z_a,z_b,z_c] is an ELEMENTWISE rescaling of
  the factors, so a CP form Σ_r λ_r u_r⊗u_r⊗u_r survives the ReLU step and the linear step is r matrix–vector products
  (O(r n²)/layer — ~free at r ≤ 64); the generated diagrams are the two-index terms R2 already has. This is the paper's
  factorized K=3 (8.2e12, 3.7× budget as published) at rank ≪ n, and the townhall (18078) notes effective rank falls
  with depth. Go/no-go for it: fit CP-r to the MC-exact distinct-index residual of κ₃(z₁₆) at layer 16 and require ≥ 80 %
  of the residual κ₃ m.s. at r ≤ 64 before writing a propagation step.

# CP-κ3 gate — low-rank propagation of the FULL third-cumulant tensor (pre-registered 2026-09-27 05:15 UTC)

Status: **criterion written BEFORE any CP / factored-source code ran.** Results appended below the next line;
nothing above that line is edited after the run. Clean-room: no participant code opened; everything below is derived
from the Hermite/Wick algebra already in `proto_r2.py` and the paper.

## Objects and identities
- K^x_abc = κ[x_a,x_b,x_c] full third-cumulant tensor of x ∈ {z15, h15, z16}; S^x = its coincident-index part (a=b or
  b=c or a=c; carried exactly by R2's two-index sector T^x, K_aab = T_ab); **D^x = K^x − S^x = distinct-index part**
  (a,b,c pairwise distinct). Identity used throughout: the R2 residual vector `distinct_true = κ₃(z16) − k3_two[T_h15]`
  (6 % of κ₃(z16) m.s., 4.3e-6 / 3.6e-6) is EXACTLY the W-contraction of D^h15 with distinct-index exclusions.
- Decomposition the factored-source family relies on: D^h15 = (Φ∘Φ∘Φ)·D^z15 [inherited, (1,1,1) Hermite diagram,
  Φ_a = Φ(μ_a/σ_a)] + G^h15 [generated at this ReLU from covariance; leading order = the path diagram
  Σ_c φ̂₂(c) (Φ∘C_:c)⊗(Φ∘C_:c)⊗e_c + perms, whose W-contraction is `k3_path`]. R2 keeps neither.

## Method (no n³ materialised; stated noise)
Fresh sample stream (seed 7+t, independent of the 1e6 refs), two independent halves A, B of N_s = 2e5 each, centred
h15 / z15 (z16 = h15 W recomputed). All tensor operations via sample contractions: D̂(·,v,v) = (1/N) Cᵀ(Cv)² − S_T̂(·,v,v)
with T̂ the SAME sample's two-index sector (so D̂ is exactly zero on coincident entries); ||D||² and ⟨D_A,D_B⟩ from the
cubed Gram (1/N_A N_B) Σ_{s∈A,t∈B} (c_s·c_t)³ − [3 Σ_{a≠b} T̂_A T̂_B + Σ_a T̂_A,aa T̂_B,aa] on 1e5×1e5 sub-blocks (unbiased
for ||D||²; error bar from the scatter over 4096-row chunks). Symmetric CP-r model M = Σ_r v_r⊗v_r⊗v_r fitted on half A
only, greedy symmetric power-method init with deflation + joint L-BFGS on the distinct-masked objective
||D̂_A − M||²_distinct; captured energy scored OUT OF SAMPLE on half B: `frac = (2⟨D̂_B,M⟩ − ||M||²_distinct) / ⟨D̂_A,D̂_B⟩`
(unbiased for 1 − ||D−M||²/||D||²; in-sample value reported for contrast). The SNR of D̂ at N_s (||D̂_A||²/||D||² − 1) is
reported; if it is > 3 the fit is noise-limited and N_s is doubled once before judging.

## Pre-stated gates (GO iff ALL pass on BOTH MLPs 1000/1001)
- **G-CP1 (representability):** out-of-sample captured fraction of ||D^h15||² ≥ **0.80 at some r ≤ 64** (r ∈ {8,16,32,64}).
  h15 is the gate object (it is what a propagation step must carry); z15 and z16 reported. Reported alongside: the
  CONTRACTED metric — slope MC/pred, corr, resid of the CP-r W-contraction (exact exclusions, 3 mat-vecs per r) vs
  `distinct_true` from the 1e6 refs — and the same for the sample oracle D̂_A itself ("CP-∞", sets the noise floor of
  this metric at N_s).
- **G-CP2 (propagation):** CP-r of D^z15 (half A), factors rescaled ELEMENTWISE by Φ from the MC-exact (μ,σ) of z15,
  W-contracted with exclusions → predicted `distinct_true`: slope ∈ **[0.9, 1.1]** and resid ≤ **0.30**, at the r that
  passed G-CP1. Reported alongside (this is the decisive decomposition for the factored-source family):
  (a) the rank-free sample oracle Φ³·D̂^z15 contracted directly (ceiling for the inherited term at ANY rank);
  (b) oracle inherited + leading generated `k3_path` (inherited + newest source); (c) tensor-level projection
  β = ⟨D̂^h15_B, Φ³·D̂^z15_A⟩ / ||Φ³·D^z15||² and the fraction of ||D^h15||² explained by the rescaled inherited tensor.
  If (b) has slope ∈ [0.9,1.1] and resid ≤ 0.30 the one-step physics of "sources born at each ReLU, transported by W,
  rescaled by Φ" is confirmed even if the CP-r truncation fails G-CP2.
- **G-CP3 (payoff, only if G-CP1 & G-CP2 pass):** 16-layer e2e R2 (no path) + rank-r factors, ≤ 10 % of 2^41 by the
  spec's op counts including R2 (≤ 2.2e11), final MSE ≤ **3e-7 on both MLPs** (1e6 refs, floor 7.2e-8). Design fixed
  now: state (μ,Σ,T) + factor matrices; linear step R2 + factor contributions to κ₃(z) diag (exact exclusions) and
  to T_z off-diag (the n³-per-factor (a=c) exclusion DROPPED, diag set exactly); factors → Wᵀ·; ReLU → Φ∘ rows; new
  factors born at each ReLU from the leading path diagram (see G-FS below for the untruncated form).
- **Cost to report** at the chosen r: per layer ≈ 6 n² r (diag contraction) + 4 n² r (sector contribution) + 2 n² r
  (transport) → r = 64: ≈ 8e8/layer = 1.3e10 total = **0.6 % of 2^41** on top of R2's 7.4 % — fits trivially.

## G-FS sub-gate — "factored sources + per-layer κ₄ scalar" end-to-end (pre-registered 2026-09-27 05:15 UTC, at the
## coordinator's request after `CLUSTER_METHOD_RESEARCH.md`; derived from the math, no participant code read)
Model (my derivation): at every ReLU layer l the distinct κ₃ generated from the Gaussian part is, at leading order, the
hub tensor S_l = Σ_c φ̂₂(c) a_c⊗a_c⊗e_c + 2 perms, a_c = Φ∘C_:c (n centres, "birth leg" A_l = diag(Φ)C, hub leg E_l = I).
Every subsequent linear layer transports both legs (A ← WᵀA, E ← WᵀE: 2 matmuls per live source) and every subsequent
ReLU rescales rows by Φ ((1,1,1) diagram). Readout of a live source into κ₃(z_i): Σ_c φ̂₂(c) A_ic² E_ic (n² per source);
into the two-index sector T_z[i,j]: Σ_c φ̂₂(c)[A_ic² E_jc + 2 A_ic A_jc E_ic] (n³ per source — used in the ceiling run
only). The hub-tensor readout omits coincident-index terms (O(1/n)); the two-index sector T (R2) and the κ₃ diagonal are
still carried exactly by R2 alongside. Untruncated cost = Σ_l 2(15−l)·2n³ ≈ 4.5e11 = **21 %** of 2^41 (this IS the
paper's factorized K=3 ~30 n³L² order; the public cluster sits at 25 %) → the shipped form must compress aged sources
(rank-r legs in a shared basis, Khatri–Rao r² readout) to ≤ 10 %.
κ₄: the cheap stand-in tested is a "memoryless" off-diagonal proxy Q̃_ab = λ_l Σ_ab (a ≠ b) with λ_l an ANALYTIC per-layer
scalar (no fitted constants) — pre-test from the cached Q refs: regress Q_x off-diag on Σ_x off-diag and on Σ_x∘Σ_x for
x ∈ {h15, z16}; the proxy is admissible only if corr ≥ 0.7 and the fitted λ is reproduced by a closed form from the
layer's own (μ,σ,Σ) to within 20 %. The diagonal κ₄ enters the mean readout as in `proto_q.py` (98.5 % ceiling).
**Gates (GO iff all hold on both MLPs):**
- **G-FS1 (ceiling, 1e6 refs 1000/1001):** the UNTRUNCATED factored-source e2e (cost ignored) reaches final MSE
  ≤ **3e-7** on both MLPs (≥ 3× over R2's 9.5–9.7e-7); reported with/without the T_z sector feedback and with/without κ₄.
- **G-FS2 (target, 1e7 refs 9000/9001, noise 7.2e-9):** a version metered at ≤ **10 % of 2^41** (spec op counts,
  compression rank stated) reaches raw final MSE ≤ **3e-8** on both (adjusted ≤ 3e-9; the public cluster is 2.13e-8 raw
  at 25 % → 5.4e-9 adjusted, so 3e-8 raw at 10 % would be 2× better adjusted). The 1e6 refs CANNOT resolve this
  (differences < 2e-7 are noise there) — G-FS2 is judged on 9000/9001 only, and estimator-vs-estimator differences
  as noise-free differentials.
- **G-FS3 (cost):** total FLOP ≤ 2.2e11 with R2 + κ₂ included; report the breakdown and the compression rank.
**NO-GO** for the family if G-FS1 fails (the one-step decomposition then has to be re-examined at G-CP2(b) before
anything is built); NO-GO for the ≤10 % target if G-FS1 passes but G-FS2 fails — then state the measured accuracy/cost
curve vs compression rank and the single remaining idea.

Symmetric CP is the wrong compression: the energy captured grows only ~+0.08 per doubling of r (0.37 → 0.60), so 80 %
would need r ≈ 500–1000 (no longer "≪ n"), and the W-contraction of a CP-64 model recovers just 55 % of the residual
vector (corr 0.74). The tensor itself is NOT the problem — the sample oracle reproduces the residual to the noise floor.

### G-FS results (factored sources, untruncated ceiling; 1e6 refs, floor 7.2e-8 included in every number)

|---|---|---|---|---|

(order-1, 5 matmuls per source-layer × 120) + 11 % sector feedback + R2 7.4 % + Q 2.8 %; transport alone is 23 % — the
public cluster's 25 % is exactly untruncated transport.

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| G-FS1 ceiling ≤ 3e-7 on both (1e6 refs) | **FAIL** (4.29e-7 / 4.14e-7; ≥ 2.2× over R2, not the required 3×) |

| G-FS3 cost ≤ 2.2e11 | **FAIL by construction**: the 10 % floor is ≈ 7 n³-matmul equivalents per layer in total; κ₂ (1.5) + R2 sector (3) + Q (2) already use 6.5, and the hub-leg transport of ONE live source costs 2 more — exact factored sources cannot carry even a single aged source under 10 % alongside R2+Q. |
κ₄ proxy pre-test (cached Q refs): Q_h15 off-diag vs Σ: corr 0.68, resid 0.51 (a Σ + b Σ² no better); Q_z16: corr 0.00
vs Σ, Q ≈ 0.37 Σ² leaves resid 0.61 → a one-scalar memoryless proxy is NOT admissible here (fails the corr ≥ 0.7 bar); the
Q-sector chain (2 matmuls) is what produced the κ₄ gain above.

### Why the ceiling stops at 4e-7 although the one-step physics is exact
Per step from exact z15 stats the hub model (inherited Φ³ rescaling + leading path source) leaves 4 % of the distinct
residual — at the noise floor. End to end it leaves 27 %: the loss is the ~25 % of EACH layer's newly generated piece
that the leading path diagram misses (the C³ triangle diagram f̂₂f̂₂f̂₂ C_ab C_bc C_ac and its relatives — not hub-form,
n⁴ to contract exactly), accumulated and transported over 15 layers. Higher path orders (C² legs) and the first-order
T×C cross sources were tested and add nothing, so the gap is the triangle family. With κ₃ at resid 0.27 and the Q chain,
the per-step readout error is ~2.2e-8 (Test-D scale), 16 steps ≈ 3.5e-7 — consistent.

### Verdict: **NO-GO** for CP-κ3 (G-CP1, G-CP2 fail) and **NO-GO** for the factored-source ≤10 % target (G-FS1, G-FS3 fail)
- Established (positive): the paper's factorized-K=3 family is REAL and complete at one step — "sources born at each
  ReLU, transported by W, rescaled elementwise by Φ" reproduces the distinct κ₃(z16) to the noise floor (slope 0.945,
  corr 0.98) from exact layer-15 statistics; e2e it buys 2.2–2.3× over R2 (9.6e-7 → 4.2e-7, noise-included) and fixes
  the κ₃ slope drift (1.36 → 1.04) and σ_z16 (1.0e-5 → 1.2e-6). This is the same family as the public 2.1e-8 cluster,
  but our untruncated implementation lands at 4e-7, not 2e-8: the difference is NOT compression, it is the missing
  triangle-class generated diagrams (25 % of each layer's source) plus whatever the cluster does for κ₄ beyond our
  Q chain — and the cluster pays 25 % of budget for it, 2.5× over the floor.
- Compression: symmetric CP-r is dead (needs r ~ n for 80 %). The Tucker/shared-basis form is closed under both propagation
  operations (U ← WᵀU, U ← Φ∘U; static r³ core) and is strictly more expressive at equal r; its representability is
  measured in `proto_cp_tucker_results.txt` (line below).
- **Single most promising remaining idea (with evidence):** stay in the factored-source family but (1) add the C³
  triangle generated diagram in a rank-compressed form — C ≈ Σ_m s_m p_m p_mᵀ at m ≤ 32 turns f̂₂³ C_ab C_bc C_ac into
  Σ_{m₁m₂m₃} (f̂₂ p_{m₁} p_{m₃})⊗(f̂₂ p_{m₁} p_{m₂})⊗(f̂₂ p_{m₂} p_{m₃}) — a CP of m³ terms whose contraction is m³ mat-vecs
  (m = 16: 4096 × 2n² = 8.6e9/layer ≈ 6 %), testable at one step from exact z15 stats against the measured 25 %-of-generated
  gap BEFORE building anything; and (2) carry aged sources in ONE shared Tucker basis (r³ core, U ← WᵀU / Φ∘U at
  2n²r per layer) so the whole source machinery costs O(n² r² + n r³) — the r² Khatri–Rao readout wall is then the only
  n³-class term and sits at ~1 matmul for r ≤ 32. Evidence for (1): the generated-part residual after the leading path
  diagram is 0.24–0.25 on both MLPs and NO hub-form term (orders 1,2; T×C) moves it. Evidence for (2): pending Tucker
  representability below; the family's e2e value (2.2×) is only worth its budget if aged sources compress to ≤ 1 matmul-eq.
  If Tucker representability at r ≤ 64 is < 0.8 as well, the honest statement is that the leader tier needs the
  cluster's 25 % budget class or a representation nobody has published, and this team should ship R2 (+Q if ≤ 10 %) and stop.

**Tucker / shared-basis representability of D_h15 (MLP 0, `proto_cp_tucker_results.txt`, out-of-sample):**
PCA(Σ_h15) basis r = 32/64/128/256 → **0.52 / 0.64 / 0.77 / 0.89** (Σ variance share 0.58/0.75/0.87/0.94); HOSVD-like oracle basis
0.55 / 0.69 / 0.82 / 0.92; SVD(T_h15) basis 0.21–0.46 (the sector's directions are NOT the distinct tensor's). Same law as CP:
≈ +0.12 per doubling; 80 % needs r ≈ 128–150 even with the oracle basis. Cost at r = 128: r³-core readout 2.1e9/layer (1.6 %) is
fine, but the exclusion Khatri–Rao term 2n²r² = 3.4e10/layer = **25 %** — the r² wall the cluster also reports (their shared
basis is rank 224–384). Conclusion for the remaining idea: shared-basis compression is viable only if the O(1) coincident-index
exclusions can be carried WITHOUT the r² unfolding (e.g. as a separately propagated two-index correction), which is the one
open algebraic question worth a day; otherwise the factored-source family is a ≥ 25 %-budget method and cannot reach ≤ 10 %.

# D21 gate — the two-index kappa3 sector is the whole gap (pre-registered 2026-09-27, after GAP_ANALYSIS.md)
Claim under test: our e2e error is the residual of the two-index kappa3 sector T (off-diag 4.5 %, diag 1.8 %) entering
(i) Cov(phi_a,phi_b) via the first-order GC term and (ii) the mean/E[phi²] readout; nothing structural is missing elsewhere.
Method (no participant code; 1e6 refs 1000/1001, same sample streams; ≤ 30 min): build all-layer MC caches of the
two-index sector T_z,l for l = 1..16 (N_s = 2e5 suffices: T noise 0.5 % ≪ 4.5 %) and of kappa3(z_l); then run
`proto_fs_e2e.fs_closure` (FS + sector fb + kappa4 := g_l sigma⁴ scalar, no Q matmuls) with the exact T_z,l (diag + off-diag)
injected at every ReLU, everything else propagated by the chain.
**G-D21-1 (payoff):** final MSE ≤ **1.5e-7** on both MLPs (1e6 refs; noise 7.2e-8 included; i.e. ≤ the exact-var_z
injection 1.68e-7/1.55e-7 within noise) AND sigma_z16 MSE ≤ **3e-7** (from 1.1e-6). PASS ⇒ D21 accuracy is sufficient
and necessary; no other family change is needed before compression.
**G-D21-2 (attribution, one step from exact z15, sample oracle as in proto_cp.py):** T_z16 off-diag from (a) the exact
sample D_h15 with exact exclusions ("CP-∞" ceiling), (b) our hub sources WITHOUT the (x,y)-slot exclusions (shipped form),
(c) hub sources WITH the exact (x,y)-slot exclusions (n⁴ here, diagnostic only), (d) (c) + Edgeworth-born sources (first
order in kappa3(z15) and kappa4(z15) at birth). Report resid vs MC T_z16 off-diag (noise floor 0.001). Decision rule:
if (c) removes ≥ 50 % of (b)'s residual → build exact exclusions (their 4-unit accounting says it is affordable at
~their 47 % cost); else if (d) does → build the non-Gaussian birth; else the triangle class is next.
**G-D21-3 (scalar kappa4, zero constants):** g_l from the chain's OWN n² quantity (mean kappa4(z) ≈ (12/n²)Σ_ab Q_h,ab
+ O(1/n²)Σ_a Q_aa, no linear-step matmul) must reproduce the MC excess kurtosis g_l to within 20 % on both MLPs at every
layer ≥ 3 (MC g: 0.009 → 0.066 monotone); PASS ⇒ drop the Q chain (−2.8 % budget) for the scalar.
NO-GO for the "D21 is the whole gap" claim if G-D21-1 fails; then the unexplained remainder is the covariance closure
itself and the next oracle is exact Sigma_z,l injection at every layer.

## D21 gate — RUN + VERDICT (2026-09-27, after pre-registration above)

Code: `research/proto_d21_cache.py` (all-layer MC caches of T_z,l, N_s=2e5, same rng stream/seed
convention as the 1e6 refs) + `research/proto_d21.py` (injected `fs_closure` run, monkeypatches
`proto_q.relu_step_sector4` to substitute the exact T and a per-layer scalar kappa4). Full numbers,
controls, and cross-validation: `research/proto_d21_results.txt`. No participant code read.

**Judged row** (kappa4 := g_l sigma^4, g_l from the chain's OWN O(n^2) reduction, no Q-chain
W-transport matmul, per "everything else propagated by the chain"):
- MLP 1000: final MSE 3.518e-07, sigma_z16 MSE 3.837e-07
- MLP 1001: final MSE 3.317e-07, sigma_z16 MSE 4.530e-07
- Thresholds: final <= 1.5e-7 AND sigma_z16 <= 3e-7, both MLPs.

**G-D21-1 verdict: FAIL** (both MLPs, both criteria; misses final MSE by ~2.3x, sigma_z16 by
~1.3-1.5x -- not a marginal/borderline result).

**Diagnostic** (MC-oracle g_l instead of the chain estimate): final MSE 2.011e-07 / 2.066e-07,
sigma_z16 4.043e-07 / 4.625e-07 -- ALSO fails both criteria on both MLPs. The failure is therefore
NOT explained by kappa4/g_l estimation error: even a near-exact kappa4 scalar does not rescue the
gate once T is the only exact quantity injected across all 16 layers (vs the one-step oracle test in
GAP_ANALYSIS.md §2, where exact upstream Sigma made the T effect nearly sufficient).

**G-D21-3 verdict: FAIL** (both MLPs; ratio of chain-estimated g_l to MC g_l is within tolerance only
at layer 2 (~0.98), already fails at layer 3 (~0.47-0.48), and decays to ~0.12-0.16 by layer 16 --
systematic, not noise). The "no linear-step matmul" mean-field kappa4 estimate loses real accuracy
once cross-layer Q_h structure accumulates beyond one layer.

**G-D21-2: NOT RUN** (time budget; both higher-priority gates already returned a clear, non-marginal
FAIL with an unambiguous next step per the decision rule below).

**Decision per the pre-registered NO-GO branch:** G-D21-1 fails -> "the unexplained remainder is the
covariance closure itself and the next oracle is exact Sigma_z,l injection at every layer." This is
the recommended next build step: inject exact (not chain-propagated) full N x N Sigma_z at every
layer alongside exact T, and re-measure. Building the (x,y)-slot exclusion machinery (G-D21-2's
original purpose) is deferred until that Sigma-level question is answered, since G-D21-1's own
diagnostic (MC-oracle kappa4 still failing) locates the gap in the covariance propagation, not in T
or kappa4 accuracy.

_(Control, mandatory before trusting the above: with T fully overwritten before
`Q.relu_step_sector4` sees it, `sources=True` and `sources=False` give FP-IDENTICAL output under
injection, max abs diff 0.00e+00 both MLPs -- confirms the injection lands at the intended point.)_

# G-K4FIT gate (pre-registered 2026-09-27, BEFORE any k4fit run)
Candidate = R2 (no path) + kappa4 := g_l sigma^4 in BOTH the covariance GC terms and the Edgeworth mean
readout, with g_l fitted from MC on train MLPs only (never 9000/9001/1000/1001), + per-layer calibration
constants refit on the same train MLPs with the g_l table in place. Judged by the mean final-layer raw
MSE on the 9000/9001 1e7 refs. The adjusted prediction = raw x max(0.1, budget fraction). PASS iff
predicted adjusted <= 1.02e-7 (the current R2+cal no-kappa4 is 1.047e-6 raw -> 1.047e-7 adjusted; the
shipped R1 is 1.185e-6 raw). Also report the variant without the refit constants (g_l table only) as the
zero-extra-constant row.

# G-COV1 / G-COV2 gates — fourth-order OFF-DIAGONAL covariance terms (pre-registered 2026-09-27, BEFORE any run)

Status: **criterion written BEFORE the experiment ran.** Results appended below the next line; nothing above that line
is edited after the run. Derivation: `research/COV_CLOSURE_DERIVATION.md` §1–5 (written first). Clean-room: first
principles + our own code + the ARC paper prose; no participant code.

## Claim under test
The accumulated off-diagonal Σ error (GAP_ANALYSIS §2: Σ_z15 off-diag MSE 3.6e-7, 13× MC noise, survives exact-T
injection at every layer in G-D21-1) is driven by fourth-order joint-cumulant terms that the closure drops:
K31_ab/6·E_G[f'''g'] + sym (the (3,1) sector) and Q_ab/4·E_G[f''g''] (the (2,2) sector, zero off-diagonal in v3).
Measured this session (1e6 caches): Q_z,off = (g_l/3)(σ_a²σ_b² + 2C²) with slope 1.00–1.01, resid 0.07 — the fourth
cumulant tensor of z is the Gaussian-scale-mixture tensor (g_l/3)Sym(Σ⊗Σ), which PREDICTS K31_ab = g_l σ_a² C_ab. The
new terms are therefore Δ_31 = (g/6)C_ab[σ_a² series(3,1) + σ_b² series(1,3)] and Δ_22 = (g/12)(σ_a²σ_b² + 2C²)
series(2,2), n² elementwise, using ONLY the already-shipped g_l table (or exact g in the oracle rows). No new constant.

## G-COV1 (one step from EXACT layer-l statistics; layers l = 8 and 15 (1-based), MLPs 1000 and 1001)
Data: `proto_cov4_mc.py` — two INDEPENDENT halves A/B, N_half = 1e5 each, deterministic prefix of the reference rng
stream (default_rng(99+t)). From each half: μ, Σ_z, T_z (two-index), K31_z, Q_z, κ3..κ6 diag of z_l, and Σ_h of h_l.
Procedure: for each closure variant V, the one-step prediction from half-X statistics is P_X = V(stats_X(z_l)) and the
same-sample residual R_X = Σ_h^MC,X − P_X (off-diagonal only). Report per entry (mean over the n(n−1) off-diagonal
entries):
  total MSE      = ½[⟨R_A,R_A⟩ + ⟨R_B,R_B⟩]
  noise floor    = ½⟨R_A−R_B, R_A−R_B⟩   (independent halves ⇒ E = noise variance of R)
  COHERENT MSE   = ⟨R_A, R_B⟩            (unbiased for the squared systematic bias, noise cancels in expectation)
  C_off gain     λ = ⟨R, P_off⟩/⟨P_off,P_off⟩ (cross-half: R_A against P_B and vice versa, averaged) — the
                 per-step relative gain error — and its energy λ²⟨P_off,P_off⟩ as a fraction of the coherent MSE;
  rank-1 share   = (top |eigenvalue|)² of the symmetric residual ½(R_A+R_B) (diag zeroed) relative to its ⟨R_A,R_B⟩
                 energy (noise inflates this slightly; reported, not gating);
  sign           = sign(λ) and the mean of R.
Variants (all with EXACT μ, Σ_z, T_z of the half; gc3 = gc4 = True):
  V0  v3-equivalent: `proto_q.relu_step_sector4` with Qz = diag(g_fit σ⁴), g_fit = the shipped table `g_table_k4fit.npy`
  V1  same with exact per-neuron κ4 diag (removes the κ4-diag accuracy question)
  V2  V1 + Δ_22 with the model Q = (g/3)(σ²σ²ᵀ + 2C²), g = exact MC g of the half
  V3  V1 + Δ_31 with the model K31 = g σ_a² C_ab
  V4  V1 + Δ_22 + Δ_31   [the JUDGED variant; = eq. (3) of the derivation]
  V5  V1 + exact MC Q and exact MC K31 (oracle ceiling for first-order fourth-cumulant terms)
  V6  V4 + second-order κ3×κ3 terms (T², T·κ3, κ3κ3) (P3 test)
  V7  V4 + own-index κ5/120 series(5,0), κ6/720 series(6,0) and κ3²/72 series(6,0), κ3κ4/144 series(7,0) + sym (H1 second-order slope test)
  V8  V0 + Δ_22 + Δ_31 with the SHIPPED g_fit table everywhere (the deployable form)
Also reported: P1 = regression of MC K31_z,off on g σ_a² C_ab (slope, corr, resid), the same for Q_z,off.
**PASS iff** on BOTH MLPs at BOTH layers: V4 removes ≥ 50 % of V1's COHERENT MSE, AND ≥ 50 % of V1's C_off-projection
energy, AND ≥ 50 % of V1's rank-1 energy (total residual also reported; if the coherent MSE of V1 is below 3× the
noise-floor uncertainty the layer is declared unresolved rather than PASS/FAIL). The sign prediction (residual
closure − MC has the sign of +(g/6)αφΦ·C for active pairs, i.e. λ_V1 > 0) is reported as a separate check.
**FAIL** otherwise. If V5 (oracle) passes but V4 does not, the model for K31 is the weak link (P1 tells which).

## G-COV2 (end to end, 9000/9001 1e7 refs, noise 7e-9)
Candidate = v3's chain (`proto_k4fit.k4_closure`: R2 no path + κ4 = g_l σ⁴ own-index) + Δ_22 + Δ_31 at every ReLU,
g_l = the shipped table `r1_data/g_table_k4fit.npy`, applied to BOTH E[φφ] (Σ_h) and E[φ²φ] (T_h).
JUDGED ROW: **uncalibrated** (g_l table only; zero constants beyond the already-shipped 16 g_l). PASS iff mean raw
final-layer MSE over 9000/9001 ≤ **5e-7** (v3 judged 9.25e-7 WITH cal; v3 uncalibrated 1.043e-6). Budget: the terms
add ~1e8 FLOP/layer of n² elementwise work (no matmul) ⇒ ≤ 10 % is assured by v3's measured 6.70 %, to be confirmed
only if a port is built. Reported, NOT judged: (a) + the existing `cal_k4fit.npy` constants unchanged (they were fitted
against a closure lacking these terms, so they may over-correct); (b) + per-layer cal REFIT on the 8 train MLPs
(new fit — flagged as such, a submission-track number only); (c) 1000/1001 1e6 refs (diagnostic, noise 7.2e-8);
(d) σ_z16 MSE and Σ_z15 off-diag MSE vs the 1e6 caches (the quantity the claim is about). G-COV2 is run only if
G-COV1 passes, or if G-COV1 fails for a stated reason that G-COV2 can still inform (e.g. one layer unresolved).

### G-COV0 (diagnostic, registered before the run at the coordinator's request; not gating)
Carrier regression, per (MLP, layer): the off-diagonal residual ΔC = Σ_h^MC − closure_V1 (exact μ,Σ,T,κ4-diag; no
fourth-order off-diagonal terms) regressed on the carriers {C_off (= Σ_z off-diag), m mᵀ (m = E[h]), (φ/σ)(φ/σ)ᵀ
(the K4-vertex proxy ⟨δδ⟩), the derived D31 pattern, the derived D22 pattern}; report coefficients, signs and the
variance explained (cross-half: patterns from half A, residual from half B). Then the discriminating check: after
projecting out the best rank-1 (m mᵀ-type) part, the fraction of the coherent residual energy explained by a single
scalar λ·C_off versus by the per-neuron-weighted D31 pattern (D31 is ∝ C entrywise with rank-2 weights
−(g/6)[α_aφ_aΦ_b + sym], so "no scalar λ works" does NOT imply an n² state is needed). Also checked numerically: the
council's rank-1 "mean-feedback" term −(m_jΔm_i + m_iΔm_j) is absent from the exact expansion (the k = 0 terms of the
series(3,0)/(4,0) rows cancel it identically — v3's k=0 identity); if a residual ∝ m mᵀ appears it has another origin.

Code: `proto_cov4_mc.py` (two-half MC, N_half = 1e5, layers 8 and 15, MLPs 1000/1001) + `proto_cov4.py`; full output
`proto_cov4_results.txt`. Same-sample residual noise per off-diagonal entry (half): 9.4e-9 (layer 8), 1.5e-9 (layer 15).

| MLP / layer | V1 coherent MSE (v3-equivalent, exact κ4 diag) | V4 (+D22+D31) coherent | removed: coh / C_off energy / rank-1 | V5 oracle (exact Q, K31) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 / 8  | 3.90e-9 | 5.49e-10 | 85.9 % / 88.1 % / 99.4 % | 2.8e-11 | PASS |
| 1000 / 15 | 1.34e-9 | 4.78e-10 | 64.5 % / 96.2 % / 93.9 % | 3.0e-11 | PASS |
| 1001 / 8  | 5.13e-9 | 6.34e-10 | 87.7 % / 94.8 % / 99.7 % | 1.3e-11 | PASS |
| 1001 / 15 | 1.37e-9 | 4.64e-10 | 66.1 % / 89.9 % / 95.9 % | 3.7e-11 | PASS |
**G-COV1: PASS** (all four rows, all three criteria). V0 (shipped g_fit table) ≡ V1 to 1 %; V8 (everything with the
shipped g_fit, the deployable form) ≡ V4 within 2 %.

Structure of the v3-equivalent one-step coherent error (G-COV0 carrier regression, cross-half): the single carrier
(φ/σ)(φ/σ)ᵀ — the leading term of D22 — explains 78 % (layer 8) / 47–54 % (layer 15) of the coherent energy; the D22
pattern itself 77–79 % / 47–53 %; the D31 pattern 7 % / 12–17 %; joint fit of the two derived patterns 87–89 % / 69–70 %
with coefficients β(D22) = 0.94–0.99 (layer 8), 0.86–0.96 (layer 15), β(D31) = 0.71–0.81; a scalar λ·C_off explains
0.0–0.1 %, m mᵀ 0.0–0.7 % (the council's "mean-feedback" rank-1 term is absent, as derived), and after removing the
m mᵀ part a scalar λ still explains 0 % — the coherent error is NOT a per-layer gain on C_off, it is the rank-1
positive (g/12)(σφ)(σφ)ᵀ Q-term plus the per-neuron-weighted D31 term. Sign: residual MC − closure has mean +3e-5
(layer 8), +6..9e-6 (layer 15): v3 UNDER-estimates Cov (the missing Q term is positive); its C_off gain λ = −(0.7–1.0)e-3
(v3 slightly OVER-estimates along C, the predicted sign of the missing D31), flipping to +(1.5–3)e-4 after D31 (the model
K31 = gσ²C over-corrects by ~25 %, consistent with β(D31) ≈ 0.75).
P1: Q_z,off vs (g/3)(σ²σ²ᵀ + 2C²): slope 0.97–1.04, resid(unit) 0.11–0.15 ≈ noise floor 0.10–0.24 (model confirmed);
K31_z,off vs gσ_a²C_ab: layer 15 slope 1.06/0.90, corr 0.70/0.59, resid 0.51/0.65 vs noise floor 0.45/0.62 (consistent
within noise); layer 8 K31 is noise-dominated at N_half = 1e5 (floor 1.4) — unresolved there. The memoryless source
Σ_c W_ca³W_cb κ4(h_c) (H2 as originally stated) is 1–2 % of the measured K31 rms with corr ≤ 0.04: WRONG mechanism.
Second-order κ3×κ3 (V6), own-index κ5/κ6/κ3κ4 (V7) and the exact marginal slope P(z>0) (V9, the H1 test) change the
coherent residual by ≤ +10 % (none helps): H1 and the κ3² block are not factors at this level.
What V4 leaves (12–35 % of V1's coherent error, 4.6–6.3e-10): the gap to the exact-sector oracle V5 (≈ 3e-11), i.e. the
non-common-mode part of Q and K31 (the C² coefficient of Q is 1.2–1.8× the model; per-neuron kurtosis scatter ±25 %).

Control: `cov4_closure(d22=d31=False)` ≡ `proto_k4fit.k4_closure` to 7e-15 (same machinery, terms cleanly switchable).

**G-COV2 verdict: FAIL** against the pre-registered ≤ 5e-7 (7.99e-7). The terms are real and free (zero constants,
n² elementwise, budget unchanged at 6.7 %) and give the best uncalibrated number this chain has produced, but they do not
carry the final MSE to the target because the final error of the R2/v3 chain is not dominated by Σ.

Diagnostics that explain why (1e6 caches, MLPs 1000/1001; `proto_cov4_e2e_results.txt`):
| chain | Σ_z15 off-diag MSE | coherent gain error λ = ⟨E,Σ_MC⟩/⟨Σ_MC,Σ_MC⟩ | σ_z16 MSE | final (1e6) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v3 | 2.59e-6 / 2.65e-6 | **−3.71 % / −3.56 %** | 1.08e-5 / 1.13e-5 | 8.75e-7 / 9.09e-7 |
| + D22 | 1.16e-6 / 1.17e-6 | +0.36 % / +0.31 % | 3.66e-6 / 3.49e-6 | 8.93e-7 / 8.36e-7 |
| + D22 + D31 | 1.19e-6 / 1.20e-6 | −0.06 % / −0.18 % | 3.81e-6 / 3.61e-6 | 8.87e-7 / 8.08e-7 |
The accumulated off-diagonal covariance bias of the shipped chain IS a coherent −3.6 % gain on Σ_z15, and the derived
rank-1 D22 term (the positive (g/12)(σφ)(σφ)ᵀ Q-vertex, transported) removes it entirely (λ → 0), halving the Σ_z15 MSE
and cutting σ_z16 MSE 3×. The final MSE moves by only −0.3e-7 on average because in the R2 chain it is dominated by the
κ3-DIAGONAL deficit (the distinct-index third cumulant that no two-index sector carries — the wall named in the Q-sector
and CP gates), and because v3's low Σ was partly cancelling its over-shooting κ3 (per-layer slope drift 1.0 → 1.4).

### The two levers, separated (coordinator's request, forum digest 504aldo #18218)
(A) **T accuracy** (root, not symptom): G-COV1 starts from EXACT T and still finds the coherent Σ_h error above — so the
Σ bias is NOT a symptom of T. But T accuracy is the LARGER lever on the final MSE: exact T at every layer (D21) takes the
FS chain from 4.2e-7 to 2.0e-7 on 1e6 refs and the v3 chain's κ3-driven remainder is what keeps it at 8e-7. Consistency
with 504aldo's rule "extra error ≈ 4.2e-6·ε²": our e2e T_h15 residual is 0.15–0.17 of the m.s. (ε ≈ 0.4) ⇒ 4.2e-6 × 0.16
= 6.7e-7 ≈ our 9e-7 − 2e-7. Their 2 % target for the κ[i,i,c] slice is the correct target; the fully off-diagonal
κ3 transport (their factored form) is the mechanism our FS prototype has at 59 % budget and our R2 lacks.
(B) **κ4-driven covariance correction** — the lever the derived terms address. Its full effect in the v3 chain: −23 % on
the final MSE (1.043e-6 → 7.99e-7 uncal), Σ_z15 gain bias −3.6 % → 0, σ_z16 3×. In the exact-T (D21) chain: see the
post-hoc block below (σ_z16 4.0e-7 → 2.9e-7, final 2.0e-7 → 1.74–1.79e-7). The structure matches 504aldo's prose
("keep the κ4 diagonal; regenerate the off-diagonal κ4 as a per-layer scalar × the pre-activation covariance") and
sharpens it: the correct off-diagonal fourth cumulants are the Gaussian-scale-mixture tensor (g_l/3)·Sym(Σ⊗Σ), i.e.
K31 = g σ_a² C_ab (scalar × covariance) AND Q = (g/3)(σ²σ²ᵀ + 2C²) (rank-1, the dominant carrier — 47–79 % of the
one-step coherent energy; a pure λ·C_off carries 0 %). No n² K4 state and no matmul is needed: the scalar g_l fixes the
whole tensor to within the 12–35 % one-step residual (the exact-sector oracle V5 leaves ~2 %).
So: (B) is worth ~1.3× on this chain and is DONE (free); (A) is worth ~4× and is the leader-tier lever; after (A) the
readout floor with κ4 = gσ⁴ is 7.3e-8 (GAP_ANALYSIS readout ladder), so the per-neuron κ4-diagonal scatter (7 % of κ4
m.s.) becomes the next 2× after that.

# G-A1 gate — lever A: the cheapest T-accurate transport of the fully off-diagonal κ3 (pre-registered 2026-09-28 ~00:35 UTC, BEFORE any run)
Role: lead theorist. Clean-room: derived from `proto_fs_e2e.py` (ours), the ARC paper prose, PROOFS.md Lemma 4 and
COV_CLOSURE_DERIVATION.md; no participant code opened. Code: `proto_leverA.py` (NEW, imports proto_r2/proto_q/proto_cov4/
proto_fs_e2e, touches nothing in `submissions/`). Design note: `LEVER_A_DESIGN.md` (written after the run).

## 1. Cost ledger of the factored-source chain as coded (`proto_fs_e2e.fs_closure`, orders=(1,), sector_fb, per source-layer)
Units: 1 unit = n³ = 1.074e9 FLOP; one (n,n)·(n,n) f32 matmul bills 2n³ − n² ≈ 2.00 units (flopscope `2mkn − mn`, f32 rate 1.0,
f64 rate 2.0, f16 = f32); budget 2^41 = 2048 units, the 10 % floor = 204.8 units. Sources are born at layers 1..15 (after the
ReLU) and read at every later layer: 120 source-layer pairs. Per source-layer as coded in `hub_readout`:
| component | matmuls (n,n,n) | units | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| leg transport P1 = WᵀA1, Qh = WᵀE (P2 ≡ P1 for same-leg sources) | 2 | 4 | 18 % |
| exclusion legs R12 = W2ᵀ(A1²), R1E = W2ᵀ(A1∘E), P3 = W3ᵀ(A1²∘E) (R2E ≡ R1E) | 3 | 6 | 27 % |
| κ3-diag readout (n·n elementwise) | 0 | 0.003 | — |
| two-index sector feedback `off` (6 matmuls as coded) | 6 | 12 | 55 % |
| Φ rescaling of 3 legs at each later ReLU, birth L1 = Φ∘C (n²) | 0 | 0.003 | — |
| **total per source-layer** | **11** | **22** | ×120 = **2640 units = 129 %** |
Base chain that stays: v3 f32 metered by flopscope = 137.2 units (6.699 %: κ2 einsum ≈ 3/layer, R2 sector 3 matmuls = 6/layer
(2 at the last layer), n² ReLU rows ≈ 0.3/layer) + the D22/D31 rows that REPLACE the Q chain (3 extra series rows in E11 and
E21 ≈ 1.7e8 FLOP/layer = 0.16 units/layer → 2.6 units) → **base ≈ 140 units (6.8 %)**; the Q chain (2 matmuls/layer, 2.8 %)
is gone. Budget left for lever A at the 10 % floor: **≈ 65 units ≈ 32 matmuls in total over 15 layers**. The untruncated
chain is 40× over that. Dominant cost: the n³ hub contraction of the sector feedback (55 %), then the exclusion legs (27 %).

## 2. Reductions (derived; each with its FLOP saving and its predicted accuracy cost)
**R-0 (exact algebra, zero accuracy cost).** For same-leg sources P2 ≡ P1 and R2E ≡ R1E, so
  off = m·[((P1² − R12)∘w) @ Qhᵀ + 2((P1∘Qh − R1E)∘w) @ P1ᵀ]  — 2 matmuls instead of 6 (−8 units/source-layer).
**R-0b (exact, age 1).** At the first readout E = I: Qh = Wᵀ (a slice of the weight matrix, free), and A1∘E = diag(A1) = 0
because C has zero diagonal ⇒ R1E = P3 = 0 exactly. Age-1 cost = P1 (2) + R12 (2) + off (4) = 8 units; age ≥ 2 = 14 units.
Untruncated total after R-0/R-0b: 15·8 + 105·14 = 1590 units = 78 % (from 129 %). Prediction: bit-identical results.
**R-1 (hub truncation — structure of the kink density).** The hub weight is w_c = f̂₂(c) = φ(α_c)/σ_c, the density of z_c at
the kink; the Frobenius energy of hub c's slice is w_c²‖a_c‖⁴ (a_c = Φ∘C_:c). 25 % of neurons are dead (|α| > 2, φ ≤ 0.05) and
the median |α| is 1.3–2.1, so the energy is concentrated on the ~25–40 % near-threshold neurons. Keep the n_h = f·n hubs with
the largest s_c = w_c‖a_c‖² (chosen at birth from the chain's own state, no constants); every leg becomes n×n_h and every
source cost scales by f. Predicted dropped energy δ(f): δ(0.5) ≈ 0.05–0.15, δ(0.25) ≈ 0.25–0.4 (to be measured from the hub
energy CDF). Accuracy cost via the forum's rule ΔMSE ≈ 4.2e-6·Δε² and Lemma 4 (incoherent accumulation ⇒ per-step factor r
gives r² on the final MSE): the sources carry Δε² ≈ 0.117 of the T_z m.s. (R2 0.16 → FS 0.043), so ΔMSE(f) ≈ 4.2e-6 × 0.117 × δ(f)
≈ 5e-8·(δ/0.1) — i.e. f = 0.5 costs ≲ 5e-8, f = 0.25 costs ~1.5e-7.
**R-2 (age gating — decay predicted from PROOFS Lemma 4).** Each of the three legs of a source is transported with the
measured one-step gain ρ_l (0.78 at l = 2 rising to 0.96 deep), so the readout ENERGY of a source of age k scales as
Π ρ⁶ ≈ 0.23–0.78 per layer: old sources decay, fastest in the shallow half. An age cap K drops all sources older than K.
Predicted share q_K of the source-carried T m.s. retained: q₁ ∈ [0.3, 0.6] (age-1 = the exclusion-corrected path diagram),
q₂ ∈ [0.5, 0.8], q₃ ≥ 0.7 — deliberately wide: the forum (504aldo #18218, prose) reports "dropping any old κ3 source costs ~4×"
at THEIR 2e-8 level, which argues against fast decay; this is the reduction the run must decide. Accuracy cost
ΔMSE(K) ≈ 4.2e-6 × 0.117 × (1 − q_K): K = 1 → 2–3.5e-7 (would roughly undo the FS gain), K = 2 → 1–2.5e-7.
**R-3 (precision).** flopscope bills f16 = f32 = 1.0 and f64 = 2.0: everything must be f32 (v3 already is), and there is NO
further saving below f32. Check only that f32 legs do not degrade the chain (prediction: < 1e-9 change on 1e6 refs).
**Rejected on paper (not run).** (i) "reuse κ2's WᵀΣ_h": the age-1 leg is Wᵀdiag(Φ)C, while WᵀΣ_h = Wᵀ[diag(Φ)Σ_zdiag(Φ) +
½(φ/σ)(φ/σ)ᵀ∘C² + …]: the higher Hermite rows are ~6 % of Σ_h at ρ ≈ 0.13 — a 6 % leg error is larger than what we try to save.
(ii) Shared low-rank basis for aged sources: PCA(Σ) at r = 32/64 captures 0.58/0.75 of C (R2_GO_NOGO Tucker block) and the
readout hits the r² Khatri–Rao wall — CP/Tucker were NO-GO. (iii) Batched/stacked transport: flopscope bills each product
exactly (forum 18184) — no saving. (iv) Strassen-type tricks: accounting, not mathematics — excluded by our own rule.
Budget arithmetic (units, base 140 included): K=1: f=1 → 260 (12.7 %), f=0.5 → 200 (9.8 %), f=0.25 → 170 (8.3 %);
K=2: f=0.5 → 298 (14.5 %), f=0.25 → 219 (10.7 %); K=3: f=0.25 → 265 (12.9 %); K=∞: f=1 → 1730 (84 %), f=0.5 → 935 (46 %).
So at ≤ 10 % the admissible configs are K = 1 with f ≤ 0.55 (and K=2 only below f ≈ 0.23).

## 3. Method (all numpy, MLPs 1000/1001 with 1e6 refs + all-layer MC T_z caches N=2e5 for diagnostics; 9000/9001 1e7 refs for the gate)
Chain = `proto_fs_e2e` structure (R2 sector + sources, orders=(1,)) with the ReLU step `proto_cov4.relu_step_ext` fed the
common-mode sectors from the shipped g_l table (`r1_data/g_table_k4fit.npy`: D22 + D31 replace the Q chain, zero new constants),
dedup readout (R-0/R-0b), hub truncation f, age cap K. FLOPs are METERED by a `Ledger` class called at every matmul /
elementwise op of the source machinery (flopscope formulas, f32 rate); the base is the flopscope-measured v3 figure + the
D22/D31 rows. Config grid: K ∈ {1, 2, 3, ∞} × f ∈ {1, 0.5, 0.25} (12 configs) on 1000/1001; per-layer T_z off-diag residual
vs MC, κ3 diag residual, hub-energy CDF at birth, source energy by age at layer 16.
**Selection rule (fixed now):** the judged config is the one with the lowest MEAN 1e6-ref final MSE over 1000/1001 among
configs whose metered total ≤ 204.8 units. It is then run once on 9000/9001.

## 4. Gates
- **G-A0 (control):** K=∞, f=1 with the dedup readout reproduces `proto_cov4_d21_results.txt` row "chain T (FS+fb), g_fit,
  +D22+D31" = 4.203e-7 / 3.490e-7 (1e6 refs) to 3 significant digits, and the dedup `off`/`diag` equal `FS.hub_readout` on
  random inputs to 1e-10 relative. FAIL ⇒ nothing below is interpretable.
- **G-A1 (the coordinator's gate, verbatim):** the selected ≤ 10 % config reaches MEAN raw final MSE ≤ **2.5e-7** on 9000/9001
  (1e7 refs, noise 7e-9 additive), total ≤ 204.8 units by the metered ledger.
  Pre-registered expectation (so the D21 lesson is not repeated): the UNTRUNCATED ceiling of this chain is 4.20e-7/3.49e-7 on
  1e6 refs = ≈ 3.5e-7/2.8e-7 noise-free → predicted ≈ 3.1e-7 mean on 9000/9001, i.e. the ceiling itself sits ABOVE 2.5e-7 at
  ANY budget. G-A1 as stated is therefore expected to FAIL for accuracy reasons unrelated to cost; the informative gate is:
- **G-A1b (cost gate):** the selected ≤ 10 % config's 9000/9001 mean MSE ≤ **1.15 ×** the K=∞, f=1 ceiling's 9000/9001 mean
  MSE. PASS ⇒ the fully off-diagonal κ3 transport CAN be carried at ≤ 10 % with ≤ 15 % loss (cost is solved; what remains is
  the family's accuracy — triangle diagrams / non-Gaussian birth). FAIL ⇒ report the frontier and the cheapest config that
  is within 1.15× (its budget is then the honest cost of lever A).
- **Frontier (reported, not gated):** all 12 configs on 1e6 refs (budget, MSE, per-layer ε²); on 9000/9001 at least 3 points:
  the ceiling (K=∞,f=1), the selected ≤ 10 % config, and the best config at ≤ 15 %; each with adjusted score
  MSE × max(0.1, units/2048).
- **Prediction checks:** hub CDF δ(0.5) ≤ 0.15; age decay q₁ ∈ [0.3, 0.6]; R-0 bit-identical; f32 legs Δ < 1e-9.
NO deletions, no git, no submissions; each command < 10 min (configs run in chunks / background).

**G-V4 verdict: FAIL.** Judged mean raw 8.0304e-7 > 7.6e-7. Every variant FAILS the gate; the covariance terms
(D22, D31) reproduce G-COV2 exactly (as expected, same machinery, same shipped g_table, uncalibrated).

**The readout term (ii) does not help — it makes every row very slightly WORSE**, not better: D22+D31 alone
7.9918e-7 -> +readout 8.0304e-7 (+0.05e-7, +0.5%); D22-only 7.8794e-7 -> +readout 7.9160e-7 (+0.04e-7,
+0.5%); readout alone vs v3 uncal: 1.0448e-6 vs 1.0429e-6 (also worse). The direction is consistent and
small across all three pairings, so this is not noise-floor scatter (1e7 refs; noise floor here is well
below 1e-9 per the G-COV2/G-K4FIT noise reports) — it is a real, reproducible, adverse sign. Two candidate
readings, both consistent with the derivation being correct as a MARGINAL (univariate) statement while the
implementation choice here was mean-only: (a) the marginal Edgeworth series is asymptotic, not convergent,
and at the actual (not asymptotically small) kappa3 magnitudes in this chain (layer 15 kappa3_z rms 8.6e-3,
COV_CLOSURE_DERIVATION.md Sec.0) the kappa3^2/72 term's sign genuinely worsens the local approximation once
higher terms (kappa5, kappa3*kappa4) that PROOFS Thm 3 lists at the SAME formal order are omitted -- adding
one same-order term without its formal partners is not guaranteed to move the truncation error in the
"right" direction; (b) the mean-only application (no matching bivariate (6,0)/(0,6) row, see the
pre-registration note above) breaks the k=0 cancellation identity that keeps the kappa4 term neutral for
Sigma/T, so part of what looks like "the readout term hurting" is really the readout/covariance mismatch it
introduces one layer downstream (mu feeds mu_z of the next layer; Sigma/T do not see the matching
correction). Not disentangled here — an open item, not resolved by this gate.

  K=∞ f=0.5 at 45.7 % (1.08×) or the energy-threshold e0.95 at 56.9 % (1.05×). **Lever A's honest cost is 45–55 % of the
  budget, not 10 %.** Everything under 15 % keeps only ~45–55 % of the FS gain.
- **Predictions vs measurement.** R-0/R-0b bit-identical: PASS (predicted). R-3 f32 legs: identical to all printed digits
  (6.8449e-7 / 6.5304e-7): PASS. R-1 hub CDF: retained energy at f=0.5 = 0.54 (layer 1) → 0.87 (layer 5) → ≥ 0.98 (layer ≥ 10)
  — the prediction δ(0.5) ≤ 0.15 holds only from layer 5 on; yet the e2e cost of f=0.5 at K=1 is ZERO (6.8485 → 6.8449e-7 /
  6.7365 → 6.5304e-7): the shallow-layer hubs that are dropped are damped 2–5× before layer 16 (Lemma 4's G_l). At K=∞,
  f=0.5 costs +8 % (3.85 → 4.16e-7): old sources are more hub-sensitive because the birth score cannot see the later
  transport. R-2 age decay: **slower than the ρ⁶ prediction** — the sector-feedback energy share by age at layer 16 is
  a1 0.26, a2 0.17, a3 0.15, a4 0.11, a5 0.09, a6 0.07 … a10 0.02 (≈ 0.75/layer, not 0.23–0.78 with a fast shallow half),
  and the T_z16 residual keeps falling to age ~10: no sources 0.170 → k1 0.140 → k2 0.121 → k3 0.103 → k6 0.072 → k10 0.051
  → k15 0.045. q₁ = (0.170−0.140)/(0.170−0.045) = 0.24 — BELOW the pre-registered [0.3, 0.6]; the forum's "every source is
  needed" is confirmed at our level too. The ε² rule holds to a factor ~1.5: Δε²(K=1) = 0.098 → predicted +4.1e-7, measured
  +2.65e-7 (1e6) / +3.4e-7 (1e7). R-4 (drop the E-leg exclusions R1E, P3 for age ≥ 2): their ENERGY is 0.3–4 % of the
  main diag term and 0.3–2.6 % of the off term (O(1/√n) as derived) but the e2e cost is +9 % (3.85 → 4.18e-7) and the
  κ3(z16) slope drops 1.02 → 0.93: small but COHERENT (a bias, not scatter) — REJECTED. Lesson: energy share does not
  price a coherent term; only the e2e run does.
- **Frontier (1e6 refs, mean of 1000/1001; full table in LEVER_A_DESIGN.md):** 6.8 % → 8.48e-7 (no sources); 8.3 % → 7.30e-7;
  9.8 % → 6.69e-7; 10.4 % → 6.45e-7; 14.6 % → 5.87e-7; 19 % → 5.35e-7; 31 % → 4.74e-7; 46 % → 4.16e-7; 54 % → 4.06e-7;
  85 % → 3.85e-7. MSE ∝ budget^(−0.35) over 10–85 %; the adjusted score MSE × max(0.1, F/B) is minimal AT the floor
  (6.1e-8 at 9.8–10.4 %) and rises monotonically above it (7.5e-8 at 14.6 %, 1.0e-7 at 19 %, 2.3e-7 at 85 %).
- **Verdict: NO-GO for "lever A at ≤ 10 %".** The transport is exact and 40 % cheaper than coded (R-0/R-0b), the
  age-1 tier with 512 hubs is the correct ≤ 10 % form (−24 % raw and adjusted vs the no-source base: 7.99e-7 → 6.08e-7,
  8.0e-8 → 6.1e-8 adjusted), but the fully off-diagonal κ3 needs EVERY source for ~10 layers and the cost of carrying them
  is n³ per source-layer with no admissible compression (CP/Tucker NO-GO; hub truncation only helps at age 1). Below
  15 % the family delivers 1.3×, not 4×.

## G-V5-PORT gate (2026-09-28) — flopscope port of v4_zc + lever-A age-1/512-hub tier

Role: Integrator. Pre-registered BEFORE any run per the recursive-learning contract.

**Lessons that shaped this gate (OPERATING_MODEL.md §5):** (1) a threshold must sit above its own oracle's attainable
value (D21) — here the oracle IS proto_leverA's own judged row (5.868e-7/6.296e-7, 199.9 units), so (a)/(b) below are
literal reproduction targets, not independent thresholds; (2) read the author's diagnostic rows yourself — re-derived
the base mismatch below by reading `model_sectors`/`relu_step_ext` directly rather than trusting the task's plain-English
"v4_zc + lever-A" framing; (3) a verification that never ran is not a verification — (a)-(f) are all executed, not just
declared; (4) energy share does not price a coherent term — the last-layer skip below is justified by an EXACT
output-independence argument (off-diagonal T is provably unused at the last layer), not by a magnitude/energy heuristic,
precisely to avoid repeating the R-4 mistake of dropping a coherent term on a magnitude argument alone.

**Base mismatch found before running anything (must be resolved here, not after a failing gate):** the task's plain
English ("v4_zc + the lever-A tier") and the task's own numeric targets (5.868e-7/6.296e-7, matching LEVER_A_DESIGN.md
§6's judged row) disagree. `proto_leverA.leverA_closure` calls `C4.relu_step_ext(mu_z, Sig_z, Tz, g*var_z**2, Qm, K31m)`
with BOTH `Qm` (D22) and `K31m` (D31) from `C4.model_sectors`; its K=0 base row (7.669e-7/8.315e-7, mean 7.992e-7) is
G-COV2's D22+D31 number, not v4_zc's D22-only number (7.6033e-7/8.1549e-7, mean 7.879e-7). **Resolution: v5 = v4_zc +
D31 (own small Horner loop, same style as v4_zc's existing D22 block, zero new constants: K31 = g_l·var_pre[:,None]·C,
S(3,1)/S(1,3) via the existing Stein-coefficient stack) + the age-1/512-hub tier**, so gate (a) is checked against
`proto_leverA`'s actual judged-config numpy code, not a mismatched base. This is a scope correction, logged here and in
OPERATING_MODEL.md §2, not a silent substitution — the orchestrator's independent re-score should diff v5 against
`proto_leverA.leverA_closure(..., K=1, f=0.5)` directly, not against v4_zc + hub alone.

**Gate thresholds (pre-registered):**
- (a) f64 port vs `proto_leverA.leverA_closure(ws, g_table, K=1, f=0.5)` at seed 9000: max abs diff of the FINAL LAYER
  output (rows[-1], i.e. the returned mean vector) ≤ 1e-10. A mutant that takes `diag(Tz_base + hub_off)` instead of
  `diag(Tz_base) + hub_diag` (the proto's `fill_diagonal(Tz, k3+hub_diag)` pattern) is the pre-registered perturbation
  that MUST fail this check — it is algebraically different only if `hub_off`'s diagonal ≠ `hub_diag` (true in general,
  since `hub_diag = 3·Σ w·Qh·(P1²−R12)` while `diag(hub_off) = Σ w·Qh·(3P1²−R12)`, off by a `2·R12` term on-diagonal).
- (b) f32 final MSE on seeds 9000/9001 vs the 1e7-sample refs within 1 % of 5.868e-7 / 6.296e-7 (LEVER_A_DESIGN.md §6
  judged row, mean 6.082e-7, 199.9 units = 9.76 %).
- (c) flopscope-METERED budget ≤ 10.0 % of 2^41 on a 1024×16 MLP, real meter (not the hand ledger in
  `proto_leverA.Ledger`, which — per the task — omits the argpartition/take cost of hub selection entirely). Report the
  exact value. If > 10 %: find exact savings first (e.g. the Sig-transpose identity S(1,3)[Fh,Fh] = S(3,1)[Fh,Fh].T,
  which is exact for the E11/Sig row since both legs use Fh — NOT for the E21/T row since F2h≠Fh); only then reduce hub
  count, and report the accuracy trade-off explicitly (never an accounting trick, rules §5.5).
- (d) residual Python time < 400 ms, measured the same way as v4 (BudgetContext residual_wall_time_s, 3 trials) AND a

- (e) non-1024×16 shapes (incl. the depth-32 smoke-test shape) reduce to the constant-free path without error. Lever
  A's hub tier is itself constant-free (computed from the model's own live statistics, no fitted g-table dependency) so

- (f) `whest validate` + `whest submit --estimator . --dry-run --yes` pass. NO real submission.

**Verdicts:** appended below after the run.

**Verdict (2026-09-28): G-V5-PORT PASS on (a),(a-mutant),(b),(c),(e),(f). (d) MIXED — FAIL under the official
subprocess runner, PASS only in-process. See the (d) row below; this is the load-bearing finding.**
`research/verify_v5_port.py` + a real `whest run --runner subprocess`:
- (a) f64 port vs `proto_leverA.leverA_closure(ws, g_table, K=1, f=0.5)`, seed 9000, final-layer max abs diff
