## G-AG — free amplitude/gain correction of the aged κ3 stack (ages ≥ 2) — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-09-29, lead prototyper; written BEFORE the C1/C2 ceilings and the γ scans were read)
Question: can a fitted low-constant gain on the aged carried terms recover a meaningful part of the carried-source-state error G-K4F located (src@8/@12 = −41/−18 % and −19/−17 %)?
Code: `research/proto_agedgain.py` (fw_closure regime A rewritten with an AGE vector and a gain table on the term WEIGHT; the read, the exclusions' S2 and the top-r score all see the scaled weight = no half-patch; `mode=read` = per-read amplitude correction, not persisted; `mode=persist` = weight × g at every ageing step of a term of age ≥ 2 → g^(age−2); the newborn's first step carries bin-0 gain 1). **Control:** gains ≡ 1 reproduces A-rinf-E 4.44521e-08 (9000) to 6 digits (run 2026-09-29). Lessons used (§5): threshold vs its own oracle; one-step ≠ e2e (ceilings are ROLLED); price by the e2e run; same-order-term-without-partners (the S2 scales with the read); selection ≠ evaluation.
- **DISCLOSURE (seen before registering):** the rolled all-bin oracle-LS fit `C3` (per layer, per age-bin, oracle gain = LS slope of the MC source on the chain's per-bin source, off-diagonal, then rolled) gave e2e 4.3895e-8 (−1.2 %) on 9000 and 3.5886e-8 (+0.2 %) on 9001, fitted gains 0.95–1.00 (slope ~0.97, the SELF_BIRTH §4 number, NOT the 0.86 of the MLP-1000 sect chain: that prior belongs to a different chain), residual of the source 0.25 → 0.243 (relative norm). I saw this before writing the rest; the stop rule below is set against it as an honest prior, not hidden.
- **Step 1 (attainability, ABSOLUTE, on the test nets — an UPPER bound because it is fit on them):** (a) rolled oracle ceilings on the exact chain: `C1` (one LS gain per age-bin per layer, newborn fixed 1), `C2` (ONE LS gain per layer on all ages ≥ 2), `C3` (all bins); (b) the direct e2e-directed ceiling of the scalar family: static γ on all ages ≥ 2, `read` γ ∈ {0.85, 0.92, 1.06} and `persist` γ ∈ {0.95, 0.98}, scored raw vs the 1e7 refs (base 4.4452e-8 / 3.5813e-8). Ceiling = best raw reduction over these rows. **Stop rule (given by the brief): ceiling < 12 % ⇒ G-AG is a NO-GO at step 1; steps 2-3 are NOT run and no constants are fitted on train nets.**
- **Step 2 (registered only for the case the ceiling clears 12 %):** forms F1 = 1 scalar (ages ≥ 2), F2 = ≤ 3 layer-band scalars (bands FIXED now: read layers 1–5 / 6–10 / 11–15), F3 = per-age g(a) with ≤ 3 constants (ages 2 / 3–5 / ≥ 6), each in `read` or `persist` mode (the mode is part of the form). Fit ONLY on train nets 5000+ (scoring vs `r1_data/train_50xx.npz['ref']`; a fit compares MSE DIFFERENCES to the γ = 1 run, which are unbiased in absolute units; refB for 5000–5005 gives the two-reference absolute MSE), quadratic in γ from a 3-point finite difference. Test on 9000/9001 vs the 1e7 refs. **PASS (all):** raw MSE reduction ≥ 8 % on BOTH 9000 and 9001 on the exact chain AND ≥ 5 % on the top-6n chain (A-r6-E, refit on its own trajectory, selection on the scaled weight); ≈ 0 FLOPs (O(H) multiplies per layer + O(n²) per S2 scaling; hand ledger ≤ 1e-4 of budget); control (wrong-sign gain 1 − δ for γ = 1 + δ, and the shuffled-layer version of F2) ≤ 2 % improvement; mutant (γ := 1 − (γ_fit − 1)) must worsen both nets. If |γ_fit − 1| < 3 % every control reads ≈ 0 and proves nothing ⇒ report NO-GO, not PASS.
- **G-AG — RUN + VERDICT (2026-09-29): NO-GO at step 1; steps 2-3 not run.** Control: gains ≡ 1 = 4.44521e-08 / 3.58129e-08 (exact; 9001 re-run on this instrument), 4.76887e-08 / 3.65215e-08 (A-r6-E). Exact chain, ceilings (9000 / 9001, Δ vs base): rolled oracle C3 −1.25 / +0.20 %, C1 −1.14 / −0.35 %, C2 −0.22 / +0.13 %; read-mode scalar γ 0.85/0.92/1.06 = +28/+7.8/+4.9 % and +33/+8.2/+7.7 % (parabola optimum γ = 0.998 / 0.991, gain 0.00 / 0.13 %); persist 0.95/0.98 = +11.8/+0.5 % and +9.4/−1.4 %. Layer-band scalars (read; 11-15 ×0.95/1.05, 6-10 ×0.97/1.03, all ×0.98): best −0.08 % (9000) / −0.11 % (9001), the rest +0.1 … +3.5 %. Top-6n: oracle C1 −2.4 / +4.7 %, C2 +0.5 / +0.1 %, read γ 0.96/1.04/1.08 all ≥ −0.02 %. **Ceiling ≈ 1–2.4 % vs the 12 % stop rule ⇒ NO-GO.** Fitted oracle gain = ramp 1.04 → 0.95 over layers 2 → 15, identical on both nets (mean ≈ 0.98; the 0.86 slope of the MLP-1000 sect chain does not hold on SBk1); the best gain lowers the source residual only 0.273 → 0.268 (≈ 4 % of energy) ⇒ the carried-state error is orthogonal to amplitude. No constants fitted on train nets; controls/mutant not run (|γ−1| < 3 % would make them uninformative). Predictions vs outcome: the brief's prior "over-shoot 15 %, gain recovers ≥ 8 %" ✗ (measured slope 0.95-1.04, ≤ 1.4 %). Lessons appended to OPERATING_MODEL §5 (2). Writeup `AGED_GAIN.md`. NOT verified by the producer.

## G-LC — in-chain learned mean-drift corrector (Puffi/mliston family) on the exact and top-6n chains — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-09-29, lead prototyper; written BEFORE any fit; data caching for FIT/VALID was already running, no model was fitted and no drift statistic other than net 0's TF profile was read)
Code: `research/lc/` (`lcchain.py` = `proto_fixedwidth.fw_closure` built by PATCHING ITS SOURCE with one hook after each layer's `relu_step_ext`; control `lc_hook=None` reproduces the plain run bit-for-bit, max|diff| = 0.0 on net 0/top-6n; `lcfeat.py` features; `lcrun.py` tasks; `split.json`). Local Mini split: 100 MLPs 1024x16, official float32 weights (convention checked: layer-0 chain mean vs truth = pure reference noise, MSE 7.0e-10 = var_h0 (0.681)/N_eff, N_eff = 9.75e8 on net 0, i.e. the ~1e9-sample claim holds; truth is stored float32 = negligible).
- **Conventions.** Layers 0-based, l = 0..15, l = 15 is the final layer; `truth[l]` = post-ReLU mean of layer l. A corrector "active from L0" acts on hooks l >= L0. Teacher forcing (TF) = after each layer the chain's mean is overwritten by the truth (chain state Sigma/T/stacks left as the chain's own). TF drift d_l = truth_l - chain_step_l(from truth_{l-1}), l >= 1. "In-chain" = hooks <= 14 only; "with-final" = hooks <= 15 (the with-final row contains the output-side case 504aldo found dead: both are reported, PASS uses with-final, and a gain that appears only from hook 15 is flagged).
- **Split (frozen, `lc/split.json`, seeded permutation `default_rng(2026092901)` of mlp_id).** FIT 60 / VALID 20 / TEST 20. VALID = 10,11,13,16,18,20,27,28,35,41,48,55,59,61,65,81,84,85,89,91. TEST = 1,3,14,19,23,24,25,26,30,31,32,44,45,71,76,82,92,93,96,99 (touched ONCE, at the end, with the frozen corrector; no TEST net's chain has been run). Net 0 (FIT) was used for the timing/control smoke test only. Independent sanity: own nets 9000/9001 (1e7 refs), reported after TEST.
- **Attainability (BEFORE fitting).** (a) TF row = truth injected after layers 1..14: by construction final MSE = the last chain step from truth_14 (net 0/top-6n: 7.4e-9 vs free 3.2e-8), i.e. every cumulative-injection row reads this same number; it is a ceiling only for a corrector that fixes the CARRIED state perfectly and touches nothing at hook 15; the cumulative rows L = 4,8,9,12,14 are therefore NOT run separately. (b) informative rows, 3 VALID nets (10, 11, 13), both chains: SINGLE reset after layer L in {4,8,9,12,14} then free run (per-layer birth/regrowth of error = which layers accumulate) and alpha-fraction cumulative injection from L in {4,9} (alpha 0.25, 0.5; approximates a corrector that removes that fraction of the drift, hooks <= 14). (c) the real bound: an IN-SAMPLE fit of each corrector form on VALID's own TF data rolled out in-chain on VALID (upper bound of the form; if it is < 20 % for a chain, PASS is unattainable for that chain and the verdict is NO-GO without a GRU). (d) cheap early kill: ridge on the F-full features from 10 FIT nets, held-out per-layer TF R^2 on VALID; if the pooled R^2 (layers >= 4) is < 0.10 (G-PAR captured ~9 %), MLP/GRU are registered as unlikely to reach 20 % and are run only as the in-chain confirmation, not tuned further.
- **Features (only quantities the estimator computes or gets with one row-reduction; no truth-derived value; superset cached, per-neuron per layer).** F-FULL (27): mu_z, sigma_z, alpha = mu_z/sigma, phi(alpha), Phi(alpha), sigma phi, chain mean mu_pre, mu_pre - Gaussian-ReLU mean (marginal correction), skew = k3/sigma^3, g (per-layer kappa4 scale), l/15, row sum of off-diag Sigma_z /sigma, row 2-norm of off-diag Sigma_z /sigma, row sum of off-diag T_z /sigma^3, row 2-norm of off-diag T_z /sigma^3, post-ReLU var_h, row sum of off-diag Sigma_h, row sum of off-diag T_h, kappa3_h diag, alpha^2, phi/sigma, layer means of alpha, sigma, |skew|, row-sum(Sigma_z)/sigma and mu_pre, and raw k3. F-LITE (9, ZERO extra flopscope reductions): mu_z, sigma_z, alpha, phi, Phi, mu_pre, k3, g, l/15. Feature standardisation is an affine map folded into the first-layer weights (0 ops).
- **Corrector forms.** M1 = F-LITE, 1 hidden layer of 16 (relu), ~0.2k params: the +60-op candidate. M2 = F-FULL, 2 hidden layers (32, 32) relu, ~2k params (diagnostic upper reference for the per-layer-shared MLP family, <= 5k cap). M3 (only if M2 in-chain VALID gain >= 10 %): per-neuron GRU across layers, hidden <= 32, <= 60k params, F-FULL input. One corrector per chain, each trained on ITS OWN chain's drift (the drift laws differ); cross-application (exact->top-6n) is reported as a diagnostic. Output added to the chain mean: mu <- mu + delta_hat, mean only (Sigma/T untouched: they are central moments).
- **Training.** Target A = TF one-step mean drift d_l (units of 1e-4). Loss U (unweighted, absolute) or S (weight 1/var_l of the per-layer FIT drift), Adam + cosine, batch 4096, early stopping on VALID TF-MSE, L0 in {4, 9}. Choice among {M1,M2} x {U,S} x {L0} on VALID in-chain final MSE (both chains, one L0/loss per form). Target B (trajectory-fitted, DAgger): roll the frozen best TF corrector out on FIT, target = truth_l - chain_step_l(corrected mu_{l-1}) (on-policy features), aggregate with A, refit; run only if the A-corrector's VALID in-chain gain is >= 3 % on the chain in question (else the drift is not a function of these features and on-policy data cannot help).
- **Hyperparameter hygiene.** Nothing is tuned on TEST or on 9000/9001. FIT standardisation/statistics only.
- **PASS (per chain, BOTH chains, TEST, frozen corrector, active L0..15).** raw final-MSE reduction >= 20 % vs the SAME uncorrected chain (paired per net; pooled ratio of means AND per-net median reported), AND reduction - max(shuffled-target control mean, layer-only baseline) >= 10 points, AND <= +1 % budget (matmul FLOPs of the corrector: stated) AND <= +60 flopscope ops for the F-LITE form (M1); if only M2/M3 pass, verdict PARTIAL: the op count is stated and the +60 bar is failed by construction, AND weights file <= 5 MB, AND 0 failed nets, AND the mutant (negated correction) is WORSE than the uncorrected chain on both chains.
- **Controls.** (i) SHUFFLED-TARGET: same form and recipe, FIT targets of layer l taken from a DIFFERENT FIT net (cyclic shift, 3 shifts: the null distribution, not one draw); it keeps the net-common per-layer drift, so it may legitimately exceed 2 % (G-PAR's constant got ~5 %): it is the null for "learned from THIS net's features", and the PASS margin above is against it. (ii) LAYER-ONLY baseline: per-layer constant + per-layer coefficient on mu_pre (32 constants, LS on FIT TF), in-chain on VALID/TEST. (iii) MUTANT: -delta_hat. (iv) F-FULL vs F-LITE gap reported.
- **Ledger.** Corrector matmul FLOPs = 2*n*(F*h1 + h1*h2 + h2) per active layer (state per form); ops per layer for M1 = stack(1) + matmul(1) + relu(1) + matmul(1) + add(1) = 5 with a constant-1 feature carrying the bias; x active layers (L0=4: 12 -> 60; L0=9: 7 -> 35). Extra reductions of F-FULL (row sums / 2-norms of Sigma_z and T_z, Sigma_h, T_h ~ 8-10 ops/layer) are what breaks the +60 bar for M2.
- **Recursive-learning lessons that shaped this design (OPERATING_MODEL §5):** threshold attainability first (a cumulative-injection table is degenerate: every row equals the last-step floor); one-step != e2e (TF drift R^2 is only a screen; the gate is the in-chain final MSE); oracle substitution (truth injection is the ceiling; alpha-fractions bound a partial corrector); fit on train only (split above, TEST once); never tune on the nets you score (no tuning on TEST or 9000/9001); a reference whose noise exceeds the quantity cannot host a relative gate (per-layer drift rms 1.6e-5..8.6e-5 vs truth noise 2.6e-5: layers 1-3 are noise-level, hence L0 >= 4); a control's threshold comes from its measured null (3 shifts, not a single draw); shared-silicon policy (CPU only, OMP <= 6, nice 19, <= 2 heavy processes).
- **G-LC ADDENDUM 1 (2026-09-29, after the top-6n VALID TF/in-chain screen of M1/M2 was read, BEFORE any M1b run; disclosed as post-hoc in design, thresholds unchanged).** Facts read first: early-kill ridge (10 FIT nets, VALID, l >= 4): pooled TF R^2 5.4 % (FULL) / 4.1 % (LITE) < 0.10, i.e. the registered early kill FIRED for a LINEAR corrector; the MLP forms are therefore run as the registered confirmation and were not tuned further (nothing was tuned: 30-epoch Adam, single seed). TF R^2 on VALID (60 FIT nets, top-6n, L0 = 9): M1 0.140, M2 0.195. In-chain VALID (top-6n, hooks L0..15, corrector trained on TF drift): M2/L0=9 22.5 %, M2/L0=4 24.1 % (n = 18), M1/L0=9 16.7 %. So the ~ +60-op LITE form (M1) is below 20 % on VALID and the +60-op bar is what separates M1 from M2. Addendum: **M1b = F-LITE + two raw row reductions rowS2_z = sum_j Sigma_z[i,j]^2 and rowT2_z = sum_j T_z[i,j]^2 (one `einsum('ij,ij->i')` each), hidden layer 32, ~0.4k params**, chosen by a greedy TF-R^2 screen on VALID (TF R^2 0.167 vs M1 0.140); op ledger at L0 = 9: 7 layers x (2 reductions + stack + matmul + relu + matmul + add) = 49 ops, at L0 = 8: 56 ops (<= 60); L0 < 8 would exceed 60 and is not eligible for the +60 bar. M1b replaces M1 as the op-limited candidate (M1 stays reported). Further forms are NOT added after this point.
- **Reading of the pre-registered injection rows (fixing the description in the pre-registration, not a threshold):** alpha-fraction injection shrinks the accumulated STATE error by (1 - alpha) per active layer (compounds to (1 - alpha)^k), it does NOT remove an alpha fraction of the one-step drift; the phrase "approximates a corrector that removes that fraction of the drift" above was wrong. The informative attainability numbers are the TF row (one step from truth_14 = 20 % of free MSE on 3 nets), the single-reset rows and the per-form in-sample/VALID in-chain rows.

## G-V10 — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-09-29, role: Integrator, folder `submissions/v10_lc/`; written BEFORE any v10 measurement)

**Scope.** `submissions/v10_lc/` = `submissions/v9_topr/estimator.py` (untouched; copied) + the frozen MIX2 learned mean-drift corrector
(`research/LEARNED_CORRECTOR.md` §4b/§6): M2 (27 features, 32-32-1) on layers 4..14, 9-feature LITE head (16-1) at layer 15, `mu = m1c + delta`
applied AFTER the layer's Sig/T are formed (prototype hook point; Sig/T use the uncorrected m1c). Weights: pickle-free `lc_weights.npz` (flopscope Module,
standardisation + output scale folded, per-layer constant/scalar features folded into a bias table computed offline) next to `weights.npz`.
Off-shape / depth != 16 -> `use_stack` guard skips the corrector. No submission; other folders untouched.
**Lessons named before design (OPERATING_MODEL §5):** the D21/T2 discipline (a threshold above its oracle's attainable value; here the prototype's
cached corrected MSEs ARE the oracle); "a verification that never ran is not a verification" + "the producer never verifies its own PASS" (exact re-run
scripts left in `research/lc/port_verify_*.py`); 131/132 (auto-routed/host-scalar warnings as errors around a `setup()`-driven predict); 156 (budget =
BudgetContext.flops_used); 175 (fidelity in the SAME quantity as the reference: per-layer MSE vs truth and final MSE); 183 (residual ~ ops x 40 us + bytes);
"BudgetContext residual != subprocess residual" (the subprocess Mini-10 run decides); `whest run --estimator` takes the FILE.
**Gate:**
(a) FIDELITY: float32 port (via real `setup()`) vs the prototype's cached corrected value (`research/lc/cache/ev_corr_top6n_MIX2_top6n_<id>_full.json`,
    `final`): on >= 5 TEST nets each within 2 % relative; pooled reduction on all 20 TEST nets (vs `free_top6n_<id>.npz`, the uncorrected prototype
    chain, exactly as `test_report.py`) within +-1.5 points of 23.29 %. Required perturbed control: the negated correction (mutant) must WORSEN the port's
    final MSE on the same nets (it must reproduce the prototype's ~-56 %, sign check). FIT nets (in-sample) reported separately, not pooled.
    Differential f64 check (port with `_DTYPE=float64` vs prototype hook, per-layer max|d| of the corrected mean) is diagnostic, not a gate.
(b) METERED: BudgetContext.flops_used fraction of 2^41 <= 41.2 % + 0.5 pt (v9 metered 41.1955 %).
(c) OPS <= 700 (BudgetContext op_log length); `whest run --estimator submissions/v10_lc/estimator.py --dataset hf://aicrowd/arc-whestbench-public-2026@v2-phase2
    --split mini --n-mlps 10 --runner subprocess --max-threads 4 --format json`: 0 failed nets, worst residual <= 0.32 s, median <= 0.27 s, wall <= 60 s.
    v9 baseline on the same command: residual median 0.222 / max 0.258 s, util 0.4120, adjusted 1.659e-8 (scratchpad/v9_mini10/out.json). The op bar is

## G-YC — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-01, lead prototyper; question: can the learned in-chain corrector REPLACE the aged-κ3 carrier?)

**Written after** measuring the chain oracles on the 3 oracle nets (10, 11, 13; ~1e9-sample refs, so the grader-style noise is ~0) and the hand ledger on 9000/9001, and **before** any FIT/VALID drift was read, any corrector was fitted or any TEST net was run. Nothing from G-YC has been read on TEST.
**Lessons named before design (OPERATING_MODEL §5):** (1) threshold above its own oracle's attainable value (D21/T2) -> the PASS bar is checked against the oracle below and the check is disclosed; (2) convert TF R^2 to e2e before gating on e2e (e2e ~ 1.15 x TF R^2 in G-LC, but that was measured where the missing effect is small); (3) a prior from another chain lineage is a hypothesis about THIS chain (G-AG) -> the G-LC R^2 0.17-0.22 is not carried over, it is re-measured on the young chain; (4) shuffled-target control keeps net-common per-layer drift (G-LC) -> report layer-only baseline beside it and gate on the margin; (5) selection = evaluation inflates (G-V9-OOS) -> fit on FIT, select on VALID, TEST touched once per frozen form; (6) hand ledger != flopscope metering (G-V6B) -> every budget below is the HAND LEDGER of proto_fixedwidth.Ledger (the same instrument as the FIXED_WIDTH frontier), and the v10 line-map estimate (~12 %) is shown as a second, optimistic adjusted column, never gated on.

**Chains** (proto_fixedwidth.fw_closure regime A, score E, excl_all; lcchain.CHAINS): `young` = `A-r0-E` (r = 0: no carried term of age >= 2; newborn k1 birth read exactly at l+1, T sector, exact exclusions, covariance, all intact), `r1n` = `A-r1-E`, `top6n` = `A-r6-E`, `exact` = `A-rinf-E`.

**Oracle / attainability rows (measured, before pre-registration):**
- Hand-ledger budget: young **17.1 %** (349.9 units), r1n 22.6 %, top-6n 44.1 %, exact 58.1 %. Raw MSE on 9000/9001 (1e7 refs, noise 7e-9 included): young 6.03e-7 / 6.13e-7 (adjusted 1.03e-7 / 1.05e-7); r1n 2.62e-7 / 2.79e-7 (reproduces the FIXED_WIDTH §5.1 row); top-6n 4.21e-8; exact 4.01e-8.
- Local Mini oracle nets 10 / 11 / 13 (1e9 refs): young free final MSE 6.74e-7 / 8.46e-7 / 7.94e-7 (top-6n on the same nets 4.47e-8, exact 4.07e-8: the young chain is ~17x worse than top-6n).
- Teacher-forced floor (truth injected after layers 1..14, only the last chain step is free): young **1.15e-7 / 1.41e-7 / 1.52e-7** (83 / 83 / 81 % removed) vs top-6n 8.2e-9 / 1.08e-8 / 7.9e-9. Single resets after L = 9 / 12 / 14 remove 29-34 / 53-59 / 81-83 %.
- **Consequence for the PASS bar:** adjusted <= 9e-9 at 17.1 % needs raw <= 5.3e-8. A corrector that fixed the carried MEAN perfectly everywhere but did nothing at layer 15 leaves ~1.3e-7 (adjusted 2.2e-8): the bar is **not attainable by mean-repair of layers <= 14 alone**; it requires the layer-15 hook to remove >= ~60 % of the young chain's last-step error (TF R^2 at layer 15 >= ~0.6) on top of a good in-chain repair. That is far above any R^2 seen so far (G-LC top-6n 0.17-0.22). The bar is kept as the user's registered bar (it is what would beat v10's predicted ~1.28e-8 by >= 30 %), but a FAIL is then the expected outcome unless the screen shows a regime change, and a partial gain is reported on its own terms in the frontier table.

**Screen (kill rule).** Fit on the 60 FIT nets (teacher-forced caches, target = truth - chain mean, early stop on VALID TF loss, the established lctrain protocol): forms M1b (L0 = 8, [32], 11 features), M2 (L0 = 4, [32,32], 27 features), AGENT17 (the Ollama-loop best row `agent_loop/log.jsonl` round 4: 17 features, [64,64], L0 = 8, 70 epochs, 3 seeds). Score VALID (20 nets) TF drift R^2 pooled over the form's layers. **KILL if the best form's VALID R^2 < 0.35**; report all three and the by-layer R^2. Report the drift variance decomposition on VALID (layers >= 4): fraction explained by FIT layer constants, by FIT layer-affine-in-mu_pre (the registered layer-only control), and the per-(net, layer) constant oracle (upper bound on "net-common drift").
**If the screen passes:** (i) pick the best form by VALID TF R^2; roll it in-chain on the 20 VALID nets (hooks L0..15, uncorrected young chain from `free_young`) and report the VALID e2e reduction; (ii) one DAgger refit round is allowed ONLY if VALID e2e < 0.8 x the TF-R^2 conversion (young's on-policy error is much larger than its TF error, so TF-only training may be off-distribution), evaluated on VALID only; (iii) TEST touched ONCE for the single frozen form: 20 TEST nets, pooled raw final MSE (uncorrected and corrected), bootstrap 95 % over nets; adjusted = corrected TEST mean raw x (17.1 % + corrector hand cost, <= 0.02 %). **PASS = adjusted <= 9e-9** (>= 30 % better than v10's predicted ~1.28e-8), with 0 failed nets. Controls on TEST (first 10 nets): shuffled-target (shift 7) corrector, **must give <= 5 % raw reduction** (the user's bar), the layer-only 32-constant corrector (reported, and the learned-minus-max(shuffle, layer-only) margin must be >= 10 points), and the negated mutant (must be worse than uncorrected).
**Frontier table (always produced, negative results valid):** chains {young, r1n, top-6n, exact} x {uncorrected, corrected} with raw (TEST pooled mean), hand-ledger budget, adjusted. top-6n / exact corrected rows are the already-reported MIX2 TEST rows (G-LC §4b, a disclosed second look); young / r1n corrected rows are G-YC's own frozen forms.
**Resources:** CPU only, <= 2 heavy processes, OMP <= 6, nice 19, `ulimit -v 12000000`; no timing runs (hand ledger only), so no TIMING_IN_PROGRESS. No submissions.

Post-kill VALID-only diagnostic (not a gate result): AGENT17 in-chain on VALID, young 6.80e-7 -> 6.55e-7 (-3.7 %), consistent with the e2e ~ 1.15-1.3 x TF R^2 conversion; DAgger precondition not met.

No young/r1n point approaches the corrected top-6n/exact region.

## G-RB2 — REBUILD stage S2 (cost): three compressibility measurements that gate the 504aldo cost stack — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-06 ~13:05 UTC, rebuild agent; written BEFORE any measurement)
**Why first.** S1's chain beats v11 on adjusted score ONLY with the full prose cost stack (7→4 collapse, age-gated shared subspace, deep Strassen). The 7→4 collapse requires that every per-source leg of the k5+feed chain be of the form {P, A, thin}: P = transported identity (the hub/propagator leg, shared by all four birth blocks since their A-legs are 3I, 1.5I, I, I), A = transported f_1∘C_z, plus thin legs. Three claims from thread 18218 must hold on OUR chain for that: (M1) the coincident adjustment leg Vadj = 3Δ21ᵀ + diag(Δ3) is A·d(t) + P·d(s) + a rank-≤16 residual ("M = P d(s) + 3A d(e) + Z Lᵀ"); (M2) the D21 feedback content in the birth legs is rank ≈ 16 ("8/16/32 → 2.17/2.14/2.14e-8"); (M3) sources older than 4 transports fit a shared n×384 basis and older than 7 a nested 224 ("rank 128 holds ≥ 0.92 of the energy after 5 transports", "3n/8 at age 4, n/4 at age 6, 7n/32 at age 7").
**Measurements (net 0, f64 hooks in `k3chain.py`, `measure_s2.py`):** M1: per layer, LS fit of Vadj's columns on (a_j, e_j), residual energy fraction and the residual's singular-value energy at ranks 8/16/32/64. M2: D21_z singular energy at 8/16/32/64 per layer AND the e2e test `feed_k5` with D21 → rank r ∈ {16, 32} inside the birth legs only (full D21 still feeds the closure). M3: per layer l, Gram eigen-energy of the stacked h-side legs [P_b | A_b] over sources of age ≥ 4 (and ≥ 7) at ranks 384 / 224, and per-source at age 1…14 at ranks 128/256/384.
**Decision rule (written now).** GO for the S2 port design if: M1 residual-rank-16 captures ≥ 99 % of the residual energy at every layer ≥ 2 (else: measure e2e the cost of dropping it before deciding); M2 e2e: rank-16 D21 legs within +1.5 % raw of full on net 0 (else rank 32; else the thin-leg claim fails and the collapse is 7→5); M3: shared rank-384 basis holds ≥ 0.95 of the age ≥ 4 energy at every layer (the e2e price is measured in the port, pre-registered then). Hand ledger target after the design: ≤ 0.40 B before Strassen, ≤ 0.34 B at Strassen d=3 (our v11 kernel). NO-GO → report S1 as the deliverable (accuracy −17.6 %, cost not shippable) and stop.

## G-RB12 — nested old-tier rank law (prose "7n/32 at age 7") in the OWN-basis port chain — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-07 ~00:00 UTC, lever-hunt agent (Fable 5.1); written BEFORE any run; only the existing own:5:384 rows (2.5119 / 4.3159 / 3.1536e-8, nets 0/2/4) have been read)
Question. v31_y4m carries every old source (age >= 5) in its OWN rank-384 basis for the rest of the chain. Thread 18218 prose (S2.4, "3n/8 at age 4,
n/4 at age 6, 7n/32 at age 7") and our G-RB2 measurement (SHARED basis, nested 224 at age 8: +0.2 % raw, net 0) say the oldest sources need less. The
own-basis port never priced it ("not pursued, ~3 units" in G-RB2 — that estimate was for the shared design where the trailing Q^T read is shared and
cannot shrink per source; in the per-source form every one of the 6r/n units per old source-layer scales with r).
Cost ledger (units = 1024^3 matmuls, B = 1024; profile `research/rebuild/prof_v31_net0.txt`): old source-layer at r = 384 costs 6r/n = 2.25 pre-Strassen,
1.72 at d = 2 (3r/n at the trimmed last layer). Source-layers with age >= 8: 36 (28 + 8 at the last layer) -> r 384 -> 224 saves ~23 units; age >= 7: 45 ->
~29 units; minus ~0.3 units per tier transition (384x384 Gram eigh + Q_b V2 + V2^T F). Predicted budget: 8:224 -> 32.37 - 1.9 = 30.5 % (adjusted x0.942);
7:224 -> 29.6 % (x0.914); 6:256,7:224 -> ~29.3 %.
Instrument. `research/rebuild/srcchain.py` extended with nested OWN tiers (`--aged own:5:384,7:224[,...]`): at age >= gate_i a source's coefficient
block F = [F_P|F_A] (r x 2n) is projected on the top-r_i eigenvectors V2 of F F^T (exact eigh in f64; the port will use the same 384x384 eigh, never n x n),
Q_b <- Q_b V2, F <- V2^T F; thin legs unchanged. Control: `own:5:384` with the new code must reproduce the stored own:5:384 rows to 1e-12 (same seeds).
Rows (f64, rf 1, nets 0/2/4): own:5:384,8:224 ; own:5:384,7:224 ; own:5:384,7:192 ; own:5:384,6:256,7:224. Raw final MSE vs the 1e9 truth.
Decision rule. Price p = mean over the 3 nets of (mse/base - 1). Projected adjusted gain G = 1 - (1+p) * budget_new/32.37 with budget_new from the
ledger above. PASS-to-port if G >= 3 % for some row with p <= 5 % on EVERY net (prefer the largest G); the ported candidate then needs the ship rule
(subprocess Mini-10 interleaved with v31_y4m, 0 failed, worst residual <= 0.36 s, adjusted <= 0.98 x v31, VmPeak <= 5.5 GB, archive validates).
KILL if every row has p > its budget saving (adjusted-negative) or a net is > 10 % worse. Residual risk, stated now: a second batched old group adds
4 sw_matmul calls per layer for l >= gate (d = 2: 45 ops each) -> +1.4-1.6 k ops, +0.04-0.06 s residual against 0.081 s headroom; mitigation rows
(if needed): old-tier d = 1 on the small group, or the 224 group at d = 2 with the 384 group at d = 1.
Prediction. 8:224 own: +0.5-1.5 % raw (shared read +0.2 %; own bases lose more, cf. +1.2 % for own:5:384 vs shared +0.2 %) -> G ~ 4.5-5 %; 7:224: +1.5-3 %
-> G ~ 6-7 %; 7:192: +3-6 %; three tiers ~ 7:224 within 1 %. Most likely verdict: PASS-to-port on 7:224 or 8:224.

Paper kills (no build, recorded so nobody retries): (L1) "contract old sources in the per-source basis instead of materialising Pz/Az = Qz F" is NOT a
re-association: the read stack needs Pz, Az ENTRYWISE (PP, PA, Az∘Y11, X12∘Af2, X21∘Af3, Pz∘Yadj are Hadamard products; the cubic monomials
Σ_k P_ik A_ik t_k P_jk etc. have an r³ core in the basis), so the F site cannot go; K→A already IS the basis contraction (3n²r vs 2n³ direct). The
5.2-pt figure in BUDGET_V41 §1 is F+K's cost, not a saving. (L2) last-layer diag: same Hadamard obstruction (Σ_k P_ik³ s_k needs every entry of
Pz). (L3a) marginals Strassen on the first product only: measured flopscope einsum cost 3.22e9 = 2.146 (cov@w) + 1.074 (symmetric-output half);
Strassen-first + plain second = ~3.45e9 → loses; needs a second Strassen site (~1000 ops) to win.
Lever (missed by the list): at every transport the newest young source has P = I (birth appends I_n, aging happens after the read), so the T site
computes wT @ I inside its Strassen call on layers 1..15. Cut: T operand [P_0..P_{k-2} | A_0..A_{k-1}] (width (2k-1)n), newest Pz := wT, C-site
right factor = concatenate([PAh^T, w], out=pooled), left reordered to match. Algebraically exact.
Prediction: T-site flops −15/108 (≈ −1.95e10 on the v41 profile) → util 0.2722 → ~0.263 (−0.9 pt), ops ±5, output identical up to f32 Strassen
rounding (f64 copy ≤ 1e-12 rel), VmPeak ≤ v43 (T arena shrinks; +1 n×8n pooled buffer).

## G-RB28 — is the learned corrector DATA-limited? Learning curve + price of more training nets — VERDICT (2026-10-07 15:45–16:00 UTC, cost-lever agent)
Learning curve (`research/lc/fit_curve.py` = fit_all.py + `--nfit k`, chain src4 caches, M2 / L0 4 / loss U / 30 epochs, VALID TF-loss checkpoint, same 20 VALID nets):
**k = 20 FIT nets → VALID TF R² 0.1228; k = 40 → 0.1344; k = 60 → 0.1376.** Increments +0.0116 then +0.0032: the curve is flattening (log-like); extrapolated
k = 120 ≈ 0.142, k = 300 ≈ 0.146. The plateau sits at R² ≈ 0.15 — the one-step drift is 85 % UNEXPLAINED by the 21 per-neuron features at ANY data size: the
corrector is FEATURE-limited, not data-limited (the "data-limited" note in LEARNED_CORRECTOR.md dates from the 10–20-net era, where the slope was 5× steeper).
Price of fresh nets (official recipe confirmed: public nets are W ~ N(0, 2/N) float32, std 0.0442 = `proto_r2.make_mlp`): MC means at 1e7 samples **882 s/net**
(`r1_data/ref_9000.log`; OMP 6–8, one heavy process); TF cache 2.1 MB/net, weights regenerable from the seed (no storage). BUT the TF targets are ONE-STEP
drifts (truth_l − pre_l), whose per-neuron sd is a few 1e-5; the 1e7 reference noise sd is 8.5e-5 per neuron (7.2e-9 MSE), i.e. the target would be
noise-dominated — 1e8 (≈ 88 min/net, sd 2.7e-5) is the minimum usable, 1e9 (≈ 24.5 h/net) matches the public refs. By Oct 13 (≈ 125 h, host shared, one heavy
slot): ≈ 45–60 nets at 1e8 (≈ 30–40 net-equivalents after the noise discount) or ≤ 5 nets at 1e9 — predicted gain from the curve: VALID TF R² +0.003–0.005,
e2e ≲ 1 % adjusted, while blocking every Mini-10 / verification run for 3–4 days. **NO-GO on net generation; nothing launched.**
What the curve says to do instead (not started; the coordinator's call): richer FEATURES on the existing 60 FIT nets — Σ_h-oriented pair/row statistics of the
step's sector terms (row sums / row norms of the κ4-sector and κ3-sector groups G4, G3 computed in `rebuild/f1_fit.py`, their diagonal shares, and the
first-order Gaussian covariance row norms), re-cached for the age-6 chain (80 nets × ~40 s ≈ 55 min), fit with the existing pipeline (minutes), e2e VALID pair
(20 min). Price ≈ 2 h of the heavy slot; the port is 21 → ~30 columns of n² ops (≈ 0.05 pt). Expected: the plateau moves only if the new features carry the
coherent Σ_h/κ4 structure G-RB25 located; G-RB27 showed a 3-scalar-per-layer model cannot — a per-neuron feature model is the next and last cheap test.

## G-RB30 / G-RB31 — pair-structured κ4 from primary prose: ARC augmented K=3 (G-RB30) and Puffi's SSC response closure (G-RB31) — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-07 ~18:30 UTC, cost-lever agent; written BEFORE any run; sources: research/lit/arc_2605.05179.txt §4.1–4.2, S.2.2, S.4.1–S.4.3; research/lit/ssc_response_closure_327725.txt §3, App. B–D; NO code repository opened)
Derivation (AUGMENTED.md): the augmented K=3 tracks η̃4 = h_{≤2}(κ4[h]) ∈ S², an n×n matrix H = tr(κ4)/(n+4) − tr²(κ4)/(n(n+4))·I + tr²(κ4)/(2n(n+2))·I
(Theorem S.2.4 eq. (6) with r=4, s=1: ch_{1,0}=1/(n+4), ch_{1,1}=−1/(n(n+4)); h0: ch_{2,0}=1/(2n(n+2))). The step computes only the (4) and (2,2) slices of κ4[h]
(S.4.1 step 2b: λ ⊢ K+1 with no singleton blocks), so tr(κ4)_kl is DIAGONAL: H_kk = [κ4_kkkk + Σ_{i≠k} Q_ik − tr²/n]/(n+4) + tr²/(2n(n+2)). κ4 ≈ g(H) = Σ_{pairs} δ⊗H;
linear step: g(H) ⊙ W = g_M(Wᵀ H W), M = WᵀW (z = Wᵀh). Slices at z (avg metric M = cI, c = mean m_i): (4) 6c H̃_ii, (2,2) c(H̃_ii+H̃_jj) [+4M_ij H̃_ij],
(3,1) 3c H̃_ij [+3M_ij H̃_ii], (2,1,1)_ijk c H̃_jk [+2(M_ij H̃_ik + M_ik H̃_ij)]. The 1/(n+4) is what G-RB26's core lacked (it set H = κ4_h: ×n). Puffi SSC:
κ4 = Σ_ab Λ_ab S(B_a,B_b), S = the three pairings; g(H) = S(I,H)+S(H,I), so the augmented object IS an SSC cross-mode (I,H) with Λ=1 — one framework:
modes {I→M, C_h→C_z, v̄I, B4 = ½(g_i+g_j)C_ij, H}, transported exactly as Wᵀ B W (1 unit each), Λ 5×5 per layer. Our lean chain = modes {C, I} with Λ fixed by g_l, κ_l.
Instrument: `srcchain_aug.py` (env AUG=off|arc|ssc, METRIC=avg|exact, FEED=keep|proj, LAMBDA=<npz>): modes from the chain's own h-state (E[h²h²] via one extra
power-cumulant series for Q_h row sums), sectors k4z / Q22 / K31 fed to the unchanged step; feed kept on the C_z leg (keep) or with amplitude projected onto the
(2,1,1) first term (proj) — a feed on new legs is priced on paper only. Control: AUG=off reproduces `f2_lean` (3.9089e-8 / 3.4658e-8 / 2.5788e-8 / 4.3529e-8 /
3.2995e-8) to 1e-12.
Bars: (G-RB30) ARC-aug zero-constant on 9000/9001 + FIT 0/2/4: no divergence (κ4_z within ×3 of the MC diag at every layer) AND pooled raw ≤ 0.90 → port;
0.90–0.97 → record as partial; else KILL. (G-RB31) SSC: Λ (and nothing else) fitted by ridge to the MC marginal κ4 of z on net 9000 ONLY (both halves, per layer,
features q_aj = B̃_a,jj from the chain's live modes); held-out e2e on 9001 and FIT 0/2/4: pooled raw ≤ 0.90 → port; the two leads are compared per util point
(ARC-aug ≈ +0.3 pt: one transport + one series; SSC(4 modes) ≈ +0.6 pt). Port bars as usual (FIT screen by adjusted, VALID-20 ≤ 0.98 / ≤ 1.10, Mini-10 vs
v49_age6k4, 6.3 GB, archive). Prediction: K4@8 ceiling 28–32 %; the (3,1)/(2,2) sectors are where the oracle said the seat is; ARC-aug recovers 5–15 %,
SSC-fitted 10–25 % (Puffi report −65 % at n=256/L=32 is a different regime and includes their other repairs).

## G-RB46 — "k-mode conditional Gaussian" ORACLE at the final layer: is the deep non-Gaussianity carried by a few dominant fluctuation modes? — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-08 ~14:50 UTC, breakthrough-hunt agent; written BEFORE any run)
Motivation: three independent hints converge — Puffi's SSC closure regenerates κ4 from ≤ 4 covariance-RESPONSE modes (separate-universe: a few large modes
modulate the bulk covariance); the P1 census "68 % of final error in a 6-D Lyapunov subspace computable from weights alone"; and the leaders' util
(0.105–0.12) equals ARC Table 1's K=2 cost (7n³L ≈ 0.11) — a covariance-only chain plus something CHEAP. If the final-layer error of a Gaussian-marginal
estimate (exact mean + variance, Gaussian shape) is removed by treating only the top-k eigenmodes of Cov(z₁₅) non-parametrically, then "K=2 chain +
k-mode quadrature/response" is a family that is both cheaper and more accurate than per-source dense-leg κ3 — the structural gap NEWREP.md could not fill.
Instrument: `research/rebuild/kmode_oracle.py` (new). Net 0 (then 2 if positive). Pass 1: N = 2^20 common-random-number samples → m̂, Σ̂ of the final
pre-activation z (f64). Eigendecompose Σ̂ → U, λ. Pass 2 (same seeds): for k ∈ {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128}: Est_k,i = mean_s G(m̂_i + Σ_{a≤k} u_ia c_a(s),
s_i²(k)), G = Gaussian ReLU-mean formula, s_i²(k) = Σ̂_ii − Σ_{a≤k} λ_a u_ia². k = 0 is the Gaussian-marginal (K=2 closure floor with EXACT moments);
k = n would be plain MC. Noise debiased by A/B halves: MSE_true = MSE((A+B)/2) − mean((A−B)²)/4 (resolution ≈ 2e-9). Controls: k = 32 RANDOM orthonormal
directions (must show ≈ 0 gain — if it gains, the gain is the sampling average, not the modes); the uncorrected f64 chain's final-layer error (2.5e-8, net 0)
and its energy fraction in span(U_1..U_k) vs the k/n null (tests the "68 % in 6-D" claim at the Phase-2 shape).
Verdict rule: PASS → new family if the debiased MSE at k ≤ 32 is < 2e-8 (below our chain) while k = 0 is ≥ 5× higher and the random-direction control
stays within 20 % of k = 0; KILL if k ≤ 32 removes < 50 % of the k = 0 error, or the random control gains as much as the eigenmodes.
### G-RB46 — RESULT (2026-10-08T14:55Z): **KILL for the k-mode family; a NEW, sharper fact replaces it.** `research/rebuild/kmode_oracle.jsonl` net 0, N = 2^20 in two independent streams, debiased.
k-mode conditional Gaussian: k0 (Gaussian marginal, exact moments) 1.8e-7 → k8 1.8e-7 → k32 1.07e-7 → k128 3.5e-7… 3.5e-8; the gain tracks the captured variance
fraction (top-32 = 59 %, top-128 = 89 %), random-32 control 2.9e-7: NO concentration of the non-Gaussianity in a few modes; the chain's error has 33 % of its
energy in the top-128 eigenmodes vs the 12.5 % null (mild). The "68 % in a 6-D Lyapunov subspace" claim does not transfer to 1024×16. Top eigenvalue 16.3
(9.6 % of the fluctuation variance) stands alone; the rest is a flat bulk. Resolution floor: the plain-MC row, which must read 0, reads 1.15e-8 (≈ 4σ of the
debias noise) — treat ≤ 1e-8 as "at the floor".
**The fact that matters:** first-order Edgeworth on the EXACT per-neuron (μ, var, κ3, κ4) of the final pre-activation reaches **1.2e-8 (floor)**; with exact κ3 and
no κ4: **3.7e-8 → ≈ 2.5e-8 after the floor ≈ our chain's 2.51e-8**; Gaussian marginal with exact moments 1.8e-7. The final-layer target is four numbers per

## G-RB49 — polarized symmetric-CP single-leg young tier with a merged D21 read — PRE-REGISTRATION + HAND-LEDGER VERDICT (2026-10-08T15:20Z, breakthrough-hunt agent; coordinator-requested; ledger written BEFORE any build; KILL rule: break-even ≤ 2 units/source-layer at ≤ +5 % raw, else no prototype)
Ledger (units = n×n×n matmul, pre-Strassen; sources: GAP504 §5 "8 young + 2·m_old legs formed per layer", srcchain docstring, G-RB23 rung 0):
- Today: 4 young sources × 2 dense legs (P = transported identity, A = transported Φ∘C_z) → T 2 + C(D21 read) 2 ≈ 4 units/source-layer, plus thin rank-4 D21-feedback legs
  (T1, T2, Z) and the κ4 feed at < 1 unit. This IS the minimum dense form of the birth tensor diag(κ)·P⊗P⊗P + Sym(P⊗P⊗A).
- Polarized single leg type: Sym(e⊗e⊗a) = [(e+a)^⊗3 − (e−a)^⊗3]/6 − a^⊗3/3 ⇒ symmetric CP with legs (e+a, e−a, a) per hub: 3 dense n×n factor matrices per
  source (all full-rank: A keeps 0.31 of its energy at rank 128 on layers 1–3, G-RB23; e±a contain the identity) → T 3 + C 3 = **6 units/source-layer = 1.5× today,
  3× the break-even.** Three-distinct-leg blocks (G11/G12/G21/feed/adj) polarize to 4 cubes each — worse still. Polarization never reduces column count; it
  only unifies leg type.
- The unified type pays only if the stacked symmetric legs compress below ≈ n columns per source. Every symmetric leg carries the identity-born e_j component,
  so a per-source basis of rank r < n loses the same energy G-RB44 measured (0.53–0.97 retained at rank 384 for age ≤ 3 → e2e ×1.07 at g4, ×1.55 at g3, cliff); a
  cross-source merge is the Tucker core n³ (NEWREP §1: Khatri–Rao wall, break-even only at r < √n). The ARC S.4.3 factorization is exactly the per-source dense
  form we run; S.8.5 adds nothing cheaper. No first-principles merge exists that is not one of the measured dead ends.
**VERDICT: KILL at the ledger (step 1); steps 2–3 (merge design, f64 prototype) not started, per the pre-registered rule.** The leaders' one-leg-cost bill therefore
cannot be a polarized form of OUR birth tensor; it must come from a different birth/closure (fewer effective legs born per layer) that no prose describes.

## G-RB60 — the ≤1.5n κ3 carrier's OBJECT: young tier exact + old tier REGENERATED from live modes (mode-locked old κ3, the κ3 analogue of the κ4 law) — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-09T18:47:51Z, fixed-width consultant (Fable 5.1); written BEFORE any run)
Derivation (why this and not a CP/Tucker recompression of the old stack): (i) in the hub-CP form the read of a source costs n²·(hubs) and its hubs have FLAT energy (hub legs V e_j, ‖V e_j‖² ≈ (1/n)Σs_i² for every j: the Lyapunov decay is in the LEFT basis, not across hubs) → keep-top-K hubs loses K/n of the content (G-FW's measured cliff); (ii) in the shared-basis Tucker form the (2,1) read of an R-dim core costs n·R³ (108 units/layer at R=384 vs ≈26 for our own-basis old tier; SECT_COST §2.1) and the core is NOT low-CP-rank (≈10n hub terms in 384 dims, generic symmetric rank ≈R²/6 = 24.6k ≫ 1.5n); (iii) the only O(n²)-per-layer object the P1 prose describes for the old content is Puffi's A716 "(2,1) history" + a fitted drift channel, and the leaders' bill equals 504aldo's young-tier-only bill to 3 digits. The κ4 tensor is ALREADY handled this way by everyone (one scalar per layer, R² ≥ 0.95 from layer 3, 18218 #5) — nobody transports κ4. Hypothesis under test: the OLD tier's z-side (2,1)+(3) read is a per-layer linear combination of O(n²) functionals of the live state (C_z, μ_z, var_z, the YOUNG read, and the exact transport of the previous layer's h-aged old (2,1) SLICE as a factored source F(M,I,I) — modes R1/R2), with per-layer scalars fitted on FIT nets and frozen. If so the carrier is: young sources (ages 1..g−1, exact, 2 dense legs each) + ≈ 15 scalars/layer; util ≈ 0.16 (g=6: the whole F/K/entry old tier ≈ 7.5 pt leaves) or ≈ 0.12–0.13 (g=4; the leaders' class).
Instrument: `srcchain_aug.py` env DUMPSRC (additive, read-only on the chain) dumps per layer the z-read summed by source age (1..5, 6+) + C_z, μ_z, var_z, Φ, f1..f3; `oldtier_oracle.py` fits per layer. Chain = the v57_azs age-6 rank-4 twin (AUG=off, AGE=6, nested 8:224, rank 4, rf 1; `aug_run.py`), FIT 0/2/4 only. Fit net 0, held-out nets 2 and 4 (frozen per-layer scalars = what a port would ship).
Bars (step 1, the oracle — decides whether step 2 is built): consumer-weighted held-out R² of the old (2,1) read (weight (f2_a f1_b)², the Σ_h coefficient) averaged over layers 6..15 for g=6 and 4..15 for g=4. Error-budget translation (BREAKTHROUGH §1 + 504aldo "no old tier = 4×" ⇒ old-tier amplitude ≈ 1.7× the current final error): residual fraction (1−R²) of the old read ⇒ raw ≈ 1 + 3(1−R²) before the head. ## G-RB62 — the adjoint/probe DUAL of the factorized κ3 chain (orchestrator's fresh angle) — PRE-REGISTRATION + DERIVATION VERDICT (2026-10-11T02:08Z, dual-angle agent (Fable 5.1); derivation and a small-n identity check only, no chain run)
§5 lessons that shaped this: "derive the break-even first; it decides WHERE a lever applies" (SECT_COST); "a cost floor is a property of the ALGEBRA it was billed in" (SELF_BIRTH); "re-read the why of an old NO-GO before re-attempting its family" (slice-only/memoryless κ3 closures at 9e-7, BREAKTHROUGH §3; young-only 6.7e-7); "a check that has never failed proves nothing" (the identity script asserts to 1e-12 and would fail on a wrong transport convention).
**Claim under test:** a pulled-back rank-1 probe formulation (v ← W_l(Φ_l∘v), contribution of layer-b births to κ3(z_l;i,i,i) = ⟨birth_b, v_i⊗v_i⊗v_i⟩) computes what the forward chain consumes at a lower leg/transport cost, or admits an O(L n³) recursion the forward chain lacks.
**Pre-registered kill rule:** KILL if (a) the dual drops nothing AND (b) its cost for ALL layers' consumed quantities is not below the forward chain's 4 units/source-layer under the same algebra.
**Derivation (`research/rebuild/g62/dual_check.py`, n=48, L=6, random W/Φ, asserts to 1e-12; ran: max|V−Pᵀ| 2.8e-16, diag 2.2e-15, slice 2.3e-15):**
1. Transport is linear: every dense leg of a source born at b is X^(b)_l = P^(b)_l X_b with the propagator P^(b)_l = M_l⋯M_{b+1}, M_m = diag(Φ_m)W_mᵀ (P = I at birth). The pulled-back probe matrix is V^(l→b) = (M_l⋯M_{b+1})ᵀ = P^(b)_lᵀ — **the dual's probes ARE the transposed P leg the chain already carries.** The "recursion that makes it O(L n³)" (V^(l→b) = M_lᵀ V^(l−1→b)) IS the forward transport of P, one product per source-layer; "one pullback per (l,b) pair" from scratch would be O(L²) EXTRA.
2. Every factor the dual contracts is an entry of a forward leg: v_i·P_j = (P^(b)_l)_{ij}, v_i·X_j = (X_bᵀ v_i)_j = (P^(b)_l X_b)_{ij}. Hence (a) the dual drops nothing and adds nothing: with the same birth blocks (G11/G12/G21/feed/adj, the D21-feedback and κ4-feed legs, the per-layer adjustment) it is the forward chain transposed — the nonlinearity of transport is not in either (both are the same linear-response Φ∘Wᵀ), and the κ3×κ3 / D21 births are birth blocks in both.
3. Cost under the same algebra, per source-layer (dense legs P, A): forward full (2,1) read = 2 transports + 2 batched read products = 4; forward DIAGONAL only = 2 + O(n²) (= the chain's existing last-layer `trim`, `d3 = Σ α (Pz∘X∘Y)`); dual diagonal only = X_bᵀV, Y_bᵀV (2) + O(n²) = 2 — identical; dual full slice = 4. The user's "≈ n per probe for the diag part" holds only for the P (=identity) factor; the X_j, Y_j factors are dense columns, so a probe costs n² and all n probes cost one n³ per dense leg — exactly the transport.
4. Where the (2,1) slice is NOT consumed the diag-only read saves 2 of 4 units — but it is consumed at every layer < 15: `proto_cov4.expectation_ext` l.110 feeds the full Tz (and Tz∘Tz second-order terms) into the Σ_h closure (SEAT #1, MODEL_ERROR); the births read rank-4 D21 (a sketch D21Ω would do, n²r) AND the adjustment block needs the full Dadj = T_h − That (dropping its residual: 19× / 4.75e-7, G-RB2); T_h itself needs Tz. Diag-only chains are the measured 9e-7 family.
**VERDICT: KILL by derivation (both kill conditions met).** The dual is an exact re-labelling of the forward chain (probe matrix = transposed propagator), same O(L² n³) total because O(L) sources are alive per layer in both; no term is dropped; the only saving (the read, 2 units/source-layer) exists only where the (2,1) slice is unconsumed, i.e. the last layer, which the chain already trims. No prototype, nothing built. Side identity recorded for G-RB63: A^(b)_l = P^(b)_l A_b exactly (A_b static at birth), so the old-tier basis need only span P — tested below.

## G-RB63 — own-tier basis from the P leg ALONE (A = P·A_b derived in that basis) at 384/224 and at reduced ranks — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-11T02:10Z, dual-angle agent; written BEFORE any run; only g61's ctrl rows (FIT 0/2/4 = 2.0700/2.2936/2.3656e-8, shipped head) have been read)
§5 lessons that shaped this: judge WITH the head (standing rule, G-RB13/33/54b/59/61 — every uncorrected pass failed net of the head); FIT-3 cannot resolve a few % → VALID-20 before any port (G-RB59b flipped sign); price a cost lever on the METERED ledger, a hand/projected saving is a projection (G-V6B); "compare a compression with the exact cost under the same algebra; derive the break-even first" (SECT_COST); re-read the old NO-GO of the family: rank cuts cliff (G-RB44 fold-at-birth, G-RB61 B1 nested 160 = +6.2 %, G-RB12 nested 224 ≈ neutral).
**Fact (G-RB62 §4):** [P|A] = P[I|A_b] — the joint entry basis (504aldo's / ours) and a P-only basis span the SAME column space (range(P), n-dim); they differ only in which r directions are kept: joint = Frobenius-optimal for both legs together, P-only = optimal for the propagator and lets A inherit (P-error)·A_b. So this is a REWEIGHTING at identical cost (the range finder's input shrinks n×2n → n×n: ≈ −0.02 units/entry, not claimed), not a new representation.
**Instrument:** f64 free-SSC twin of v58_ne (G-RB61 env: `SSC=1 AUG=ssc FREE=1 QCOEF=qcoefF2.npz LAMBDA=lambda_F2.npz AGE=6 RANK=4 NESTED=1 GSCALE=0.92 LCSCALE=1.2`) with the shipped head `corr_sscf_MIX2`; new flag `PBASIS=1` in `srcchain_aug.py` (entry L = P only; nested eigh on F_P only; default off = bit-identical); `g62/eval63.py` (eval61 + `OWN_R`); runner `g62/run_g63.sh`; rows → `g62/eval63.jsonl`.
**Arms (FIT 0/2/4):** ctrl re-run on net 0 (must reproduce g61 ctrl 2.0700e-8 to the printed digit — a free control; a mismatch voids the session); PB384 = PBASIS at own 6:384 / nested 8:224; PB320 = PBASIS at 320/192; PB256 = PBASIS at 256/160; J320 = joint basis at 320/192 (the same-rank control that tells whether a P-only basis tolerates a smaller rank BETTER than the joint one).
**Bars:** (i) PB384 pooled FIT raw ≤ 0.99 vs ctrl → VALID-20 (there: pooled ≤ 0.98 AND ≥ 12/20 nets improve → candidate at identical util; adjusted = raw ratio once the port's metered util is shown equal ±0.1 pt). (ii) a reduced-rank arm is a COST lever only if pooled FIT raw ≤ 1.00 AND it beats the joint same-rank control by ≥ 2 %; projected price (old-tier F/K + entry sketch ∝ r: 384→320 ≈ −0.3 to −0.5 pt ≈ −1.5 to −2 % adjusted) × raw must be ≤ 0.97 to earn a VALID-20; a metered port price is required before any ladder. (iii) KILL if PB384 > 0.99 AND no reduced arm meets (ii).
**Prediction:** PB384 1.00 ± 0.01 (a reweighting of an already Frobenius-optimal joint truncation; the whole basis machinery is worth 2.7 % raw, ERROR_BUDGET, so even a perfect reweighting is below bar (i)); PB320 ≈ J320 ≈ +2–4 %, PB256 ≈ +6–10 % (G-RB61 B1 pattern). Prior for any bar PASS ≤ 15 %. Cost: 13 runs × 24 s ≈ 6 min, one process, OMP 8, load-gated.
- **G-RB63 — RESULT (2026-10-11T02:12–02:20Z, `g62/eval63.jsonl`, `g62/run_g63.log`, load 5–13): KILL on every bar; no VALID-20, no port.** ctrl net 0 re-run = 2.0699922e-8 = g61 ctrl to the printed digit ✓ (session valid; ctrl pooled 6.7292e-8). PB384 (P-only basis, 384/224): 2.1108 / 2.3631 / 2.3955e-8 → **pooled 1.0208** (per-net 1.020 / 1.030 / 1.013; bar ≤ 0.99 ✗). PB320: 2.2403 / 2.5012 / 2.4859 → **1.0740**; J320 (joint, same ranks): 2.1877 / 2.4214 / 2.3729 → **1.0376** — the P-only basis tolerates a smaller rank WORSE than the joint one (needed ≥ 2 % better; ✗). PB256: **1.265**. Prediction check: PB384 "1.00 ± 0.01" → 1.021 (outside, and in the harmful direction); J320 "+2–4 %" → +3.8 % ✓; "PB320 ≈ J320" → +7.4 % vs +3.8 % ✗; PB256 "+6–10 %" → +26 % ✗ (the P-only basis cliffs ~3× faster). Reading: the joint basis is Frobenius-optimal for [P|A] = P[I|A_b]; spending all r directions on the propagator lets the A leg inherit (P-error)·A_b, and A is the leg the read values most (the (2,1)-born terms carry as much energy as the diagonal-born ones, BREAKTHROUGH §3) — so the reweighting moves the error INTO the consumed leg. A tuned weighting [P·d(w_P)|A·d(w_A)] is not run: the whole basis machinery is worth 2.7 % raw (ERROR_BUDGET), below the 3 % adjusted bar even if perfect (bar-on-ceiling, G-LC). Together with G-RB44/60/61/12 the old-tier basis question is closed in both directions (what to span, and at what rank).

## G-RB64 — LENS_E idea G: the exact-gating κ3 transport seat (trivariate orthant vs ΦΦΦ on the (1,1,1) sector) — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-11T02:55Z, dual-angle agent (Fable 5.1); written BEFORE any run; coordinator-specified bars)
§5 lessons that shaped this: the noise lesson (rows with MC noise need the A/B two-half debiasing; size N against the quantity under test and report noise next to signal — G-RB48/G-K4F/G-V9-OOS); "an exact layer is a free noise-floor instrument" → the debiased ms ⟨E_A E_B⟩ and the noise ms ⟨(E_A−E_B)²⟩/2 are reported for every row; "a one-step oracle of a CHANNEL does not test its STATE" → this is a ONE-STEP seat measurement, and any e2e claim needs the head arm (standing rule); "re-read the why of old NO-GOs": G-RB26/37 (κ4 transports), G-RB27/36 (Σ_h), G-V4 (same-order term without partners) — this gate measures a term CLASS before any form is built.
**Claim under test (LENS_E §2.G):** the chain gates every transported κ3 leg by f1 = Φ, so its (1,1,1) sector is (Φ⊗Φ⊗Φ)∘κ3_z while the exact first-order coefficient is the orthant probability P3(a,b,c); first order in C the difference is ≈ 8 % rms relative at depth and is not in any gate. Agent's addendum (same class, measured together and split off): the Gaussian-born (1,1,1) κ3_h has C-cycle terms (f2f2f2 C_ab C_bc C_ca, …) that no hub-separable birth block carries — also O(ρ).
**Instrument:** `research/rebuild/g64/orthant_oracle.py` — official FIT nets 0/2/4, layer l = 12 (z_12 → h_12 → z_13), N = 2^19 total as two independent halves of 2^18, f32 forward / f64 moments. Per half: truth_i = κ3[(δh@W)_i]; gated_i = κ3[((δz∘Φ)@W)_i] (ΦΦΦ-gated transport of the FULL κ3_z); (3)+(2,1) slices of each from the sample T_h, T_z (the chain holds these exactly via the adjustment); births111 = (1,1,1) part of the chain's birth blocks (G11/G12/G21/feed at P = I, FULL-rank D21, this half's MC-exact μ, var, C_z, D21, κ_12) read as full-minus-slices; **E_i = (truth − sl) − (gated − sl) − births111.** Gaussian-surrogate arm (z_G ~ N(μ, Σ_z), same N): E^G = exact Gaussian-born (1,1,1) − the chain's Gaussian block (3, A1, A1∘f2) → the cycle-class truncation. Regressors (G1/G2 linearised): r_k = 3E[δv_k δu δu] − slices with v_k = (δz∘ψ_k)@W, ψ ∈ {g∘(Cg), g∘ΣC², α, Φ, g, 1}.
**Noise sizing (pre-registered):** per-neuron κ3 noise at 2^18 ≈ √(6 var³/N); the debiased ms ⟨E_A E_B⟩ over 1024 neurons resolves rms ≈ noise/√32 ≈ 1 % of κ3 rms (LENS_E's 0.5 % estimate at var 0.17; recomputed from the measured var_z). The 3 % bar is attainable; the per-neuron R² is read cross-half (fit on A, score ⟨(E_A−p)(E_B−p)⟩ vs ⟨E_A E_B⟩).
**Bars (coordinator):** (K1) debiased rms(E) < 3 % of rms(κ3_z13) on the pooled nets → KILL (the seat is too small); (K2) seat ≥ 3 % but cross-half R² < 0.2 on the G1/ψ_k regressors → KILL G1/G2 (bulk-dominated, n⁴ exact — recorded with the number). (P) seat ≥ 3 % AND R² ≥ 0.2 → f64 prototype of the gate form on the free-SSC twin + shipped head, FIT 0/2/4 → VALID-20 → v62 → ladder. Secondary read (not a bar): share of E that is the Gaussian-born cycle class (E^G) vs the orthant/κ3-induced remainder.
**Prediction:** seat real at 5–10 % of κ3 rms (prior 55 % that K1 is NOT met: the two O(ρ) terms are the same size as the Tz seat MODEL_ERROR measured); E^G ≈ half of it; R² on the per-neuron gate forms ≤ 0.1 (prior 80 % for K2) because both corrections couple PAIRS through C_ab, which a per-neuron gate cannot express. Joint PASS prior ≈ 10 %. Cost: ≈ 5 min/net, one process, OMP 8, load < 16 before each net.

## G-RB65 — LENS_E idea H: learned PAIR-LEVEL Σ_h corrector (per-neuron-modulated sector features), A/B-debiased — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-11T03:00Z, dual-angle agent; written BEFORE any run; coordinator-specified bar)
§5 lessons that shaped this: G-RB27/G-RB36 read R² ≈ 0 because the per-entry residual sits at the 1.3 % MC floor — the cross-half product ⟨r_A r_B⟩ is the instrument that sees a coherent residual below the per-entry noise (G-RB48's calibration lesson; "a reference whose noise exceeds the quantity under test cannot host a relative gate" → the ratio is read on debiased energies); teacher-force BOTH inputs and outputs from the SAME half so the input noise does not enter the cross product as a bias (G-K4F: an oracle that replaces a transported state must be priced with its own noise structure); "convert the oracle gain into the e2e gain before registering an e2e bar" → this gate registers only the oracle bar, the e2e bars come after; the standing HEAD-arm rule for any e2e step.
**Claim under test (LENS_E §2.H):** the coherent part of the Σ_h closure residual (SEAT #1, 38 % of the final error) is a per-entry bilinear form in per-neuron Hermite features times the step's own matrix terms: δΣ_h(a,b) = Σ_k u(a)ᵀΘ_k u(b) M_k(a,b), M_k ∈ {C, C², C³, T, Tᵀ, T∘C, 1}, u ∈ {1, Φ, g, f3, f4, κ3f3, κ4f4} (343 constants shared across layers 4–14), util +0.1 pt.
**Instrument:** `research/rebuild/g65/sigh_pair_fit.py` on the existing 3e5-per-half oracle caches (`mc_oracle_9000/9001_N300000.npz`): residual r_h = Σ_h^{MC,h} − `relu_step_ext`(MC-exact μ, Σ_z, T_z, κ4, Q, K31 of half h), off-diagonal; ridge fit on 9000 half A (α by the 9000 cross-half objective); score on the HELD-OUT net 9001: explained fraction of the coherent energy 1 − ⟨(r_A−p)(r_B−p)⟩/⟨r_A r_B⟩ pooled over layers 4–14 (p from pooled inputs), and the same for the one-step var_z effect diag(Wᵀ r W).
**Bars (coordinator):** held-out explained coherent energy < 10 % → KILL; OR the fitted δΣ raises the one-step var_z coherent error on 9001 → KILL. PASS → e2e on the free-SSC twin, FIT 0/2/4: uncorrected ≤ 0.95 AND shipped-head arm ≤ 0.98 → VALID-20 → v62 → ladder.
**Noise sizing:** per entry noise 1.3 % of Σ_h rms vs coherent ≲ 0.3 % (G-RB36); ⟨r_A r_B⟩ over 1.05e6 entries resolves ≈ 1.3 %/√1e6·√2 ≈ 0.002 % — the coherent energy is readable; the fit's noise-absorption is ≈ 1.3 %·√(343/1.15e7) ≈ 0.007 % rms, negligible against 0.3 %. Caveat recorded in advance: coherent energy per layer may come out ≤ 0 on some layers (noise); the pooled number is the bar.
**Prediction:** coherent residual rms 0.2–0.4 % of Σ_h; held-out explained fraction 0–8 % (prior 85 % for KILL — G-RB27's "pair-structured, quenched" reading: the residual's structure is in WHICH pairs, carried by the transported κ3/κ4 content, not by per-neuron Hermite factors); a PASS would most likely come through the 1-matrix (u uᵀ) block. Cost: ≈ 25 closures + 22 design matrices (2.9 GB each, one at a time) ≈ 10–15 min, one process, after G-RB64 finishes (one heavy process at a time).

The chain's one-step (1,1,1) error E (truth − ΦΦΦ-gated − exact slices − full-rank chain births): debiased coherent rms **1.42e-4 / 1.92e-4 / 1.54e-4 = 1.39 / 1.37 / 1.82 % of κ3 rms, pooled 1.47 %** (bar K1: < 3 % → KILL). ## G-RB67 — floor-argument audit (brief: "find the flaw in our floor argument"): is the young A leg a (diag + rank-r) image of the P leg, i.e. does a young source need ONE dense transport (3 + 4r/n units) instead of two (4)? — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-11T19:50Z, floor-audit agent (Fable 5.1); written BEFORE any oracle number was read; only the chain's own per-layer state capture (`rb67/rb67_capture.py`, an lc_hook dump of μ_z/Σ_z/Φ) is run concurrently)
**Derivation that motivates it (full text: `research/review/LENS_F_floor_audit.md`).** In `srcchain.py` the birth legs are P = I and A = f1∘Cz_off (`A1 = f1[:,None]*Cz`, Cz zero-diagonal) and BOTH are aged by the same linear map X ← Φ∘(WᵀX), so at every later layer A_s^l = P_s^l · a_s with a_s = D_s Cz_off^s STATIC (exact; the identity G-RB62/63 used). The young-tier bill of 4 units/source-layer is {transport P, transport A, read with right factor Aᵀ, read with right factor Pᵀ}. If a_s = d(c) + U_r V_rᵀ + (dropped bulk), then A = P d(c) + (P U_r) V_rᵀ: the A transport becomes a thin transport (r/n), the dense Hadamard partners are formed at n²r, and BOTH reads collapse onto the right factor Pᵀ (Aᵀ = d(c)Pᵀ + V_r (PU_r)ᵀ, thin) → 3 + 4r/n units/source-layer. This is the only re-association of the young tier that drops a dense product; Horner over right factors Pᵀ, the full-rank shared basis A_s = G_l G_sᵀ (Gaussian-linearised), polarization (G-RB49) and the Tucker/x-coordinate forms all return ≥ 4 (LENS_F §2). It is NOT the leaders' 2x: at r=128 the saving is 0.5 of 4 on the young tier (≈ 39 % of util) → ≤ 5 % util, adjusted ≥ 0.95 even on a PASS. It is run because it is the one unmeasured cost assumption in LENS_E §0/§1 ("4 units/source-layer irreducible") and it is cheap.
**Instrument (f64, FIT 0/2/4 only, generator caches not used):** (1) `rb67_capture.py`: `srcchain.src_closure` with the shipped-twin config (rank 4, rf 1, aged own:6:384,8:224 — `results.jsonl` cfg `src_r4_rf1_agedown:6:384,8:224`) and an lc_hook that returns the mean UNCHANGED and dumps μ_z, var_z, Σ_z, Φ per layer. (2) `rb67_oracle.py`: for each layer s: eigh of Σ_z^s, Frobenius energy of Cz_off captured by off(top-r) and by the (diag + rank-r) fit, r ∈ {32,64,128,256}; for layers l ∈ {6,10,14} and sources of age 1..4: rebuild P_s^l = W_lᵀΦ_{l−1}⋯Φ_{s+1}W_{s+1}ᵀ and A_s^l = P_s^l a_s exactly, A_r = P_s^l a_s^r, and the G11 read `read_block(3, P, A, A∘f2_s)` → per-source rel Frobenius error of the (2,1) read and of its (3)-diagonal, and the error of the SUMMED young-tier read (the quantity the ε²-law prices).
**Bars (504aldo F71: extra MSE ≈ 4.2e-6 ε², ε = rel rms error of D21; ≤ 10 % raw ⇒ ε ≤ 2.2 %; the young tier is the majority of D21 at depth):** PASS (the lever exists, port it as a 3-unit young source, priced ≤ 0.95 adjusted) if the summed young-tier read error ≤ 2 % at r ≤ 128 on all three layers and all three nets. WEAK if ≤ 2 % only at r = 256 (saving 3+1 = 4: no lever; recorded as the leg's effective rank). KILL if > 2 % at r = 256 on any net/layer: the A leg is as full-rank as P, the Hadamard wall stands at 4 units, and LENS_E's cost side is confirmed with a measured number.
**Prediction:** Σ_z^1 = W_1ᵀW_1 is Wishart-like (rank 128 ≈ 50–60 % of the off-diagonal Frobenius energy); at s ≥ 6 the leg Gram concentrates (92 % trace in 128 modes after 5 transports, 504aldo §2.4) → 90–97 % energy → rel error 0.2–0.3. Expected: **KILL** at every r ≤ 256 (rel error ≥ 0.1), the (diag+rank) fit no better than ×1.5 over plain truncation. Prior of PASS: 10 %; of WEAK: 15 %.
Lessons used (OPERATING_MODEL §5): "a cost floor is a property of the ALGEBRA it was billed in" (SELF_BIRTH) — list which billed products recompute something the chain already holds (A = P·a_s); "measure the MSE-vs-retained curve under the best score out to the exact limit" (G-FW) — r up to 256 and the exact limit; "a truncation is a committed, persistent error" (SECT_COST) — the truncation is applied at birth and transported, never re-truncated; "energy share does not price a coherent term" — the bar is on the READ (the consumed object), not on ‖a_s‖_F; one heavy process, OMP ≤ 8, ulimit -v 16000000, load < 16 before each step.
**G-RB67 KILL (A-leg (diag + rank-r) compression; `rb67/rb67_oracle.jsonl`, FIT 0/2/4, 2026-10-11T19:52Z).** Summed young-tier (ages 1–4) (2,1)-read relative Frobenius error at l=6/10/14: r=128 **0.29 / 0.15–0.16 / 0.09–0.10**; r=256 **0.13 / 0.08 / 0.06–0.07** (all three nets within ±0.01); bar 2 % → KILL at every r on every net and layer (prediction "KILL, rel error ≥ 0.1" confirmed; the per-source read error is ≈ 1.5 × the A-leg norm error, D3 diagonal ≈ 0.9 × the (2,1) error). Two structural reads that correct LENS_E: (1) **Σ_z is NOT a flat bulk at depth**: the residual off-diagonal Frobenius energy after rank-128 is 0.40 at s=0 (W₁ᵀW₁, Wishart-like, as predicted) but **0.025 at s=6, 0.008 at s=10, 0.003 at s=14** (rank 256: 0.001–0.005 for s ≥ 6); top-1 eigenmode 0.4 % → 8.7 % of the trace from s=0 to 14; var_z falls 2.0 → 0.18 (the generator is sub-critical, variance halves every ~4 layers). The (diag + rank-r) fit improves plain truncation by ≤ 10 % relative: the diagonal is not the obstacle. (2) **A 0.4 % leg-energy residual is a 10 % read error and a ×1.5–2 raw loss by the ε²-law**: the read needs the legs to ≈ 1 % in NORM (1e-4 in energy), which no energy-ranked compression reaches below r ≈ n — this is the mechanism of every rank cliff in the ledger (G-FW knee 5n, 504aldo "one notch lower is a cliff", G-RB44). Equal weight after transport (brief (b)) confirmed for the young read: per-source off-diagonal read norms at l=14 are 0.54 / 0.51 / 0.48 / 0.41 for ages 1–4 (net 0; nets 2/4 alike) — a 25 % decline over 4 ages, not an exponential one. Control: the capture's uncorrected finals 2.5549 / 4.1877 / 3.3144e-8 reproduce the G-RB60 session control to every digit. No port; the 4-units/young-source-layer bill stands as measured (3 + 4r/n needs r ≥ n at the 2 % bar).

## G-RB68 — brief (a) directly: the (1,1,1)-induced share of the next layer's (2,1) read, and whether that missing term has any low-rank or parallel structure a slice-only closure could carry — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-10-11T20:10Z, floor-audit agent; written BEFORE the run; capture extended to dump T_h and Tz per layer)
**Object.** With the chain's own h-side slice T_h^{l−1} (closure output; (3)-diagonal exact), the memoryless (slice-only) transport is M = F(I, I, V), V = 3 T_offᵀ + diag(D3) (DESIGN step 5: M's slices equal T_h exactly, its (1,1,1) part is zero) → at layer l legs (W_lᵀ, W_lᵀ, W_lᵀV) and read R_mem = read_block(1, W_lᵀ, W_lᵀ, W_lᵀV). The chain's actual read Tz^l (all sources, full (1,1,1) content) minus R_mem is exactly the (1,1,1)-induced part Δ^l of D21^l — the term every slice-only recursion must regenerate.
**Measurements (FIT 0/2/4, layers 2–14):** (i) share_l = ‖off(Δ^l)‖_F / ‖off(Tz^l)‖_F (norm; energy = share²) and the (3)-diagonal share; (ii) rank profile of Δ^l: energy in its top-8/32/128 singular directions (the Sym(u⊗V) / low-rank-closure family can carry only that); (iii) cos²(Δ^l, R_mem) and cos²(Δ^l, Tz^l) over off-diagonal entries (a scalar rescaling of the memoryless read captures cos²); (iv) the per-entry rms of Δ vs Tz.
**Bars (ε²-law 4.2e-6 ε², raw ≤ 3e-8 at the brief's bar ⇒ ε_total ≤ 5 %).** ALIVE (a slice-only chain could reach the brief's bar with a cheap closure) if at every layer ≥ 8: share ≤ 0.05, OR top-32 singular energy of Δ ≥ 0.90, OR cos²(Δ, R_mem) ≥ 0.90 (then a scalar per layer recovers it). KILL otherwise: a slice-only recursion needs Δ to ≤ 5 % absolute, i.e. R² ≥ 1 − (0.05/share)² on a quenched full-rank n×n target. **Prediction:** share 0.40–0.50 (504aldo F65: 18–23 % of D21 ENERGY lost ⇒ norm 0.42–0.48; e2e 9.1e-7 = 4.2e-6 × 0.46²), top-32 energy ≤ 0.15, cos² ≤ 0.3, Δ per-entry rms ≈ half of Tz's → **KILL**, with the slice-only ε reproduced independently of 504aldo's chain. Prior ALIVE ≤ 5 %.
Lessons used: "re-read the WHY of an old NO-GO before re-attempting its family" (the memoryless closure is dead end #2 — this measures its mechanism on OUR chain rather than re-running it e2e); "price a dropped term by its e2e run, never by its norm" — here the norm feeds the MEASURED ε²-law, not an energy-share heuristic; "verify an agreeing oracle harder": the prediction agrees with 504aldo, so the (3)-diagonal share and the rank profile are independent reads of the same object.
**G-RB68 KILL ((1,1,1)-induced share of D21; `rb67/rb67_slice.jsonl`, FIT 0/2/4, layers 2–14, 2026-10-11T19:58Z).** ‖off Δ‖/‖off Tz‖ = **0.40–0.49 at every layer on all three nets** (energy 0.16–0.24: 504aldo F65's 18–23 % reproduced on our chain by an instrument that never ran theirs); diagonal share 0.25–0.34; cos²(Δ, R_mem) < 1e-3 (Pythagorean: ‖R_mem‖²/‖Tz‖² + share² = 0.80 + 0.20 = 1.00) so the best per-layer scalar on the memoryless read is λ = 0.99–1.01 and buys nothing. None of the three ALIVE conditions holds (share ≤ 0.05: no; top-32 ≥ 0.90: no; cos² ≥ 0.90: no) → KILL. **Prediction partly WRONG, recorded:** Δ is not a flat bulk — its top-8/32/128 singular energy is 0.10/0.31/0.71 at l=2 and **0.51/0.77/0.93 at l=14** (predicted ≤ 0.15 at 32), concentrating with depth like Σ_z (Tz's own top-32: 0.67 → 0.96). It does not rescue (a): the bar needs Δ to ≤ 10 % of its norm (R² ≥ 0.99); the top-128 subspace (93 %) is a property of the tensor contracted with the NEXT layer's W and costs ≥ the dense tier to obtain (Tucker core 15nR³ ≈ 15 units at R=128, lossy), and live-state regressions read ≤ 0.5 (G-RB60). ε²-law check: a slice-only chain has ε = 0.45 → +8.5e-7 (504aldo 9.1e-7, Puffi 9.8e-7). Full audit: `research/review/LENS_F_floor_audit.md`.

## G-RB72 — input-space (Wiener/Hermite) chaos formulation of κ3: the order-1 mean-Jacobian + order-2 (Stein/Price) Hessian form vs the cumulant chain — PRE-REGISTRATION + DERIVATION (2026-10-12T01:35:46Z, chaos-lens agent (Fable 5.1); written BEFORE any oracle number was read; only the rb67 state captures (chain's own μ_z/var_z/Σ_z/Tz per layer, FIT 0/2/4) and the official FIT weights are inputs)
§5 lessons that shaped this: "a dual that re-labels a linear transport is the same algorithm; cost it by writing the pulled-back object in terms of what the forward chain already carries before building anything" (G-RB62); "re-read the why of an old NO-GO before re-attempting its family" (LENS_E §L killed input-basis chaos by the 0.73/layer linear-chaos retention, G-RB46 by the k-mode oracle; this gate tests the FULL-basis, degree-2 form the brief says was untried); "a threshold must sit above its own oracle's attainable value" (noise sizing below); "verify an agreeing read harder than a disagreeing one" (the chain-vs-truth row is the control that must reproduce the known ε ≈ 2 % before any chaos row is believed).
**Claim under test (brief):** with x the only randomness, κ3(z_l) can be formed from the order-1 chaos J^l = E[∂z_l/∂x] (recursion J^l = J^{l−1} diag(Φ_{l−1}) W_l, one n³ per layer) and the order-2 chaos E[∇²z_{l,i}] = Σ_k Σ_b c_{ikb} J^k_b J^k_bᵀ (Stein/Price), giving κ3_iii ≈ 3 J^l_iᵀ E[∇²z_i] J^l_i = 3 Σ_k Σ_b c_{ikb} (J^l_i·J^k_b)²; the (1,1,1) content is then "represented through inner products, not a tensor", possibly at O(L n³).
**Derivation (to be checked numerically by the oracle; written before the run):** with P^{k→l} the chain's propagator (z_l-index × h_k-index) and a_k = Φ_k∘C_z^k the chain's birth A leg: A^{k→l} = P^{k→l} a_k = **J^lᵀ J^k + P^{k→l}(Φ_k∘R^k)**, R^k := C_z^k − J^kᵀJ^k = the part of the layer-k covariance in x-chaos degrees ≥ 2. Hence the chaos (1,1,2) term 3 Σ_b c_{ikb}(J^l_i·J^k_b)² with c_{ikb} = P_{ib} f2_k(b) is EXACTLY the chain's Gaussian hub birth block Sym(3 P⊗A⊗A∘f2) read on the diagonal, with A replaced by its degree-1 part G_{lk} = J^lᵀJ^k; its (2,1) read is the same two contractions (G∘G f2)Pᵀ + 2(P∘G f2)Gᵀ. Forming G_{lk} is one n³ per (l,k) — the same bill as transporting A — so the chaos form is a cost-neutral, LOSSY re-association (drops P(Φ∘R^k)), and the all-layer version is O(L² n³) like the chain (every (l,k) pair needs its own G and P). The cumulant chain IS a chaos expansion — in Hermite polynomials of each layer's Gaussian z_{l−1} (per-layer base, fast convergence), the brief's form expands in Hermite polynomials of x (global base; LENS_B §5 measured 0.73/layer retention of the degree-1 chaos).
**Instrument:** `research/g72/chaos_oracle.py` — official FIT nets 0/2/4; chain state from `research/rb67/state_000{0,2,4}.npz` (μ_z, var_z, Σ_z, Tz per layer; the shipped-twin f64 chain, uncorrected finals 2.5549/4.1877/3.3144e-8 reproduced by rb67). Mean-field J^k from the chain's Φ (J^0 = W_0; J^k = J^{k−1} diag(Φ_{k−1}) W_k). At l ∈ {6, 10, 14}, for EVERY source k < l: P^{k→l} by exact transport; R_C = read_block(3, P, A_C, A_C∘f2_k) with A_C = P(Φ_k∘off C_z^k) (chain's Gaussian hub block, exact), R_J the same with A_J = P(Φ_k∘off(J^kᵀJ^k)) (= J^lᵀJ^k off the hub diagonal; the chaos form). Sums over all k: T_hubC, T_hubJ. MC truth: two independent halves of 2^18 x-samples (f32 forward, f64 accumulation, two passes per half with the same stream: means, then centred Tz_l = E[δz²δzᵀ], Σ_z^l, and J_MC^l = E[x δz_lᵀ]) at the three layers in one forward sweep per pass. Rows per (net, l): debiased cross-half ms of off(T − T_truth) and of diag(T − T_truth) for T ∈ {T_chain (captured Tz_l), T_hubC, T_hubJ}, noise ms ⟨(Δ_A−Δ_B)²⟩/2; rel ‖off(T_hubJ − T_hubC)‖/‖off T_hubC‖ summed and per source age; ρ_k = ‖off(J^kᵀJ^k)‖_F/‖off C_z^k‖_F (mean-field, every k) and ρ_l^MC from J_MC (l = 6, 10, 14); ‖J_MF^l − J_MC^l‖/‖J_MC^l‖.
**Noise sizing (pre-registered):** per-entry Tz noise per half ≈ var_z^{1.5}/√N: l = 14 (var 0.18) 1.5e-4 vs off rms ≈ 3.5e-3; l = 6 (var ≈ 0.6) ≈ 1e-3 vs off rms ≈ 1e-2. The debiased cross-half ms over n² entries has noise ≈ noise²/n ≈ 2e-11 (l=14) / 1e-9 (l=6) against the chain's own error ms (ε ≈ 2 %) ≈ 5e-9 / 4e-8 → the chain-vs-truth control is resolved ≥ 20× at every layer; a chaos row ≥ 3× the chain's error is resolved trivially.

(K2, accuracy) debiased rms of off(T_hubJ − T_truth) > debiased rms of off(T_chain − T_truth) at l = 10 and 14 on ≥ 2 of 3 nets → the brief's question (3) "is order-2 chaos enough" answered NO → KILL. (P) BOTH K1 ≤ 0.10 AND K2 reversed (chaos error ≤ chain's) → price the all-layer form against ≤ 0.15 util and, only if it prices, an f64 full-chain prototype (bar raw ≤ 2.5e-8 at priced util ≤ 0.15 with a shipped-head or FIT-refit head arm) → v70 → ladder. ## G-RB81 — adjoint linear-response κ3 correction of the FINAL MEAN on a K=2 trajectory (DeepSeek-V4-Pro consult C1, `xfam/xfam_deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.out`) — PRE-REGISTRATION + DERIVATION (2026-10-13T19:02Z, adjoint-mean agent; written BEFORE any code ran; only the consult, LENS_E/F/G, G-RB62 and srcchain.py were read)
§5 rules/lessons that shaped this: standing rules 1 (head arm before any port), 3 (bars/kill/prediction stamped here first), 5 (price every arm myself in n³ units), 6 (decompose before you build: the arm ladder below IS the decomposition), 7 (a falsifier that must fail: adjoint≡forward identity + sign-flipped mutant), 14 (bg.sh, bg_audit); G-RB62 "a dual that re-labels a linear transport is the same algorithm — cost it by writing the pulled-back object in terms of what the forward chain carries"; LENS_E §J "O(L n³) exists for the FINAL layer only"; LENS_G §2 "a backward sweep is G-RB62, O(L²) either way"; lesson "re-read the why of an old NO-GO before re-attempting its family"; prior-art pointer (scout): Ni, arXiv:2507.21497 (adjoint path-kernel, covector reuse for a terminal statistic).
**Derivation (term count; done before any run).** Mean map on the K=2 trajectory: δm_z^{l+1} = W_{l+1}ᵀ δm_h^l, δm_h^l = Φ_l δm_z^l + (f3_l/6)∘diag κ3_z^l (+ var/C terms, path (b)). κ3 transport on frozen gates: κ3_z^{l} = κ3_z^{s}[G,G,G] + births, G = G_{s→l} (rows g_i). The final-mean first-order response is δm_L = Σ_l H_{L←l} diag(f3_l/6) diag3(κ3_z^l) = Σ_s Σ_{l≥s} Σ_i H_{L←l}[:,i](f3_{l,i}/6) ⟨b_s, g_{s→l,i}^{⊗3}⟩. The adjoint state at birth layer s is therefore Σ_{l≥s} Σ_i c_{l,i}(g_{s→l,i})^{⊗3} with VECTOR coefficients c ∈ Rⁿ: **n(L−s) rank-1 cubes with distinct directions**. A pullback through M_s keeps the term count and cannot merge terms (the cube is nonlinear in its direction; the linear mean propagator H only moves coefficients). Sweep cost Σ_s (L−s) n³ ≈ L²n³/2 — the forward source chain's order. The consult's "K_l = M_lᵀK_{l+1}M_l" (an n×n congruence) is a type error for a cubic kernel; its "K_l = n rank-1 cubes, one matmul/layer" is exact ONLY when every read sits at one layer (l = L): that is G-RB62 / LENS_E §J (final-layer κ3 read, ≤ 8 % ceiling at n = 1024, L = 16). The carried-mean error (75 %) enters through the INTERMEDIATE reads l < L, which the cheap form drops. Ni 2507.21497's covector reuse makes cost independent of the number of SOURCES for a SCALAR terminal statistic; here the statistic is an n-vector and there are only ≈ L sources, and the shared contractions ⟨b_s, (g_{s→l,i})^{⊗3}⟩ are per-(s,l) work in either direction — forward mode (the source chain) is already the right ordering.
- **(a) κ3-induced κ3 transport:** the D21-feedback births (G11 T-parts, G12, G21 via T1/T2) and the adj block from T_h are LINEAR in κ3 → they belong inside the adjoint of T_l; their adjoint maps a cube onto slice-type terms x_a⊗x_a⊗y_a (one new family of n terms per output-read per layer), not onto cubes → no rank-1 closure. LENS_G measured ≈ 75 % of one-step κ3 content as κ3-induced, so a congruence-only Wᵀdiag(Φ) adjoint misses most of the transport. The gate-derivative effect of κ3 on later means is first order but is inside H (mean propagator).
- **(b) covariance path:** first order (κ3 (2,1) slice → Σ_h via (T/2)S(2,1) → later var_z → f0(m, var) and Φ) and needed (dropping T is K=2's 1.3e-7 calibration point, LENS_E §3.3). Its adjoint per output is ∂m_{L,j}/∂Σ_h^l, an n×n matrix → n³ per layer for the n-vector target, pulled back at n⁴ (or n² slice-type terms per read layer). Not cheap.
- **(c) second order:** κ3×κ3 births ≤ 1 % of the T term at n = 1024 (LENS_E §3.3); at n = 128 κ3 is ≈ √8× larger relative, so it is MEASURED here (A5 − A4), not assumed.
**Instrument:** `research/g81/` — `srcchain_g81.py` = a COPY of srcchain.py's src_closure with mask flags (srcchain.py untouched), module globals N/D set to the small net; synthetic nets W ~ N(0, 2/n) (in,out), no bias, x ~ N(0, I) (the official generator law), seeds 0/1/2; κ4 OFF in every arm (g = 0, κ = 0 → k4z = 0, feed u = 0) so every K3−K2 gap is κ3 only; no aging, D21 rank = n (exact factored chain). MC truth: 2^22 samples per half, two independent halves, debiased MSE = mean_i (m_i − t^A_i)(m_i − t^B_i). Arms (final layer h_{L−1} mean): **A0** K=2 (κ3 ≡ 0); **A1** the consult literally = Gaussian births (G11 hub at P = I with Y = A∘f2, + Gaussian-slice adj from T_h(Tz=0)), ΦΦΦ congruence transport, κ3 read at the FINAL layer only, Σ_h Gaussian (exactly linear: K=2 trajectory frozen); **A2** = A1 + κ3 diag read into the mean at EVERY layer; **A3** = A2 + κ3-induced births (D21 blocks + adj from the full T_h); **A4** = A3 + Tz into the Σ_h closure (full first-order content); **A5** = srcchain at κ4 = 0, rank n (full nonlinear). A2–A4 also reported as central-difference linear responses (ε = ±1e-3 on all births; first-order part) next to the unlinearized arm; A5 − A4lin = (c). Extra arm n = 128, L = 16 (A0/A1/A5) before any extrapolation (registered bias: at L = 8 the final read is a LARGER share than at L = 16, so A1 at small L overstates).
