**Question.** G-RB67 killed the W-INDEPENDENT rank-r basis (6–10 % summed young (2,1)-read error at r=128/256, bar 2 %). Does a basis built from the known next-layer read operator do better? Instrument `research/rb82/rb82_oracle.py` (reuses rb67 state_{0,2,4}.npz, FIT nets 0/2/4, layers 6/10/14, f64; module code not modified).
**Quantities.** (T1) slice test: ‖off(Tz_l − proj)‖/‖off(Tz_l)‖ with proj = Q Qᵀ Tz Q Qᵀ (two-sided; one-sided also logged). (T2) read test: next read R_mem(l+1)=read_block(1,Wt,Wt,Wt V(Th_l)) recomputed with Th_l ↦ Q Qᵀ Th_l Q Qᵀ vs the full-Th read, off-diagonal rel. Frobenius. (T3) G-RB67-frame young-tier test: exact read_block(3,P,A,A∘f2) summed over ages 1–4 vs the read with rows of A ↦ Q Qᵀ A (Y recomputed), (2,1) off-diagonal rel. err.
**Bases (all k = 32/64/128).** W-ADAPTED-R: right singular vectors of M_{l+1}=W_{l+1}ᵀ diag(Φ_l) (input side, the physically correct one); W-ADAPTED-L: left singular vectors as the consult literally states (z_{l+1} side; logged as the literal reading); RANDOM orthonormal (control, must be far worse); W-INDEP: top-k eigenvectors of Σ_z,l (the G-RB67 covariance basis, same projection frame) and G-RB67's own logged r=128/256 numbers for reference.
**Bar / kill.** KILL if the best W-ADAPTED basis gives off-diagonal read error > 2 % at k ≤ 128 on ANY net/layer in T2 or T3 (T1 reported, not a gate). PASS (to step 2) only if ≤ 2 % at k ≤ 128 on ALL 9 net×layer cells AND RANDOM is ≥ 5× worse. Validity falsifiers: (V1) k = n projection reproduces the exact read to ≤ 1e-9; (V2) RANDOM control worse than W-ADAPTED or the instrument is flagged broken; (V3) W-INDEP T3 within the right order of G-RB67's logged 6–10 %.
**Prediction (self-labelled).** FIT nets are N(0, 2/n)-like at init-scale ⇒ M_{l+1} has a near-quarter-circle singular spectrum with no dominant subspace ⇒ top-128 of 1024 holds ≈ 30–40 % of ‖M‖²_F and the projected read error is ≳ 30 % at k=128 (T2/T3), RANDOM ≈ 80–95 %, ADAPTED not meaningfully better than W-INDEP. Expected verdict: **KILL**.
**Cost question (answered by term count after the run, in n³ units).** See RESULT.
**Self-label line:** see G-RB82 — RESULT below.

### G-RB82 — RESULT (2026-10-13T19:31Z, rb82 agent): **KILL. The W-adapted basis is no better than a random basis on the slice and the A-leg read (97–99 % error at k ≤ 128 vs bar 2 %); only the next-read recompute shows any adaptation (T2 82–86 % at k = 128), still 40× over the bar.** Instrument `research/rb82/rb82_oracle.py` (rows `rb82/rb82_oracle.jsonl`, log `rb82/oracle.log`), nets 0/2/4 × layers 6/10/14, f64, 9 cells; ranges below are min–max over the 9 cells.
**Bug caught in the first run (mine):** `rel()` was given the projected object instead of the difference, so errors read 4–16 % and GREW with k — the monotonicity tell; fixed, file deleted, re-run. All numbers below are from the fixed run.
Spectrum of M_{l+1}=W_{l+1}^T diag(Φ_l): top-32/64/128 singular directions hold only 16 % / 30 % / 51 % of ‖M‖²_F (σ1/σ128 = 1.4) — a near-flat quarter-circle, no dominant subspace for any k ≤ 128.
| basis (k=128) | T1 slice, 2-sided | T2 next-read recompute | T3 young-tier A-leg read (ages 1–4 summed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| W-ADAPTED-R (right sv of M, physically correct) | 0.988–0.991 | 0.815–0.857 | 0.968–0.975 |
| W-ADAPTED-L (literal consult) | 0.990–0.993 | 0.978–0.989 | 0.970–0.977 |
| RANDOM (control) | 0.992–0.994 | 0.980–0.990 | 0.970–0.976 |
| W-INDEP (Σ_z,l eigenbasis, row frame) | 0.927–0.945 | 0.893–0.946 | 0.344–0.471 |
At k = 32 / 64 adaptR T3 = 0.993–0.995 / 0.986–0.990; T2 = 0.974–0.988 / 0.930–0.958. Validity: V1 (k = n reproduces) ≤ 4.5e-15 ✓; V2 (random control worse) ✓ but only by a hair — adaptR ≈ random on T1/T3, i.e. the adapted basis carries ≈ no information about where the slice/legs live (it beats random only on T2, 0.82–0.86 vs 0.98); V3: G-RB67's own logged column-compression numbers (summed young (2,1) read, r = 128/256) are 0.092–0.291 / 0.060–0.129 across the same 9 cells; my W-INDEP row-projection control is a DIFFERENT frame (rows of A, not columns of a_s) and gives 0.34–0.47 at k = 128, so it does NOT reproduce 6–10 % (not claimed to; G-RB67 stays the reference). The ordering that matters is robust: ADAPTED ≈ RANDOM ≫ worse than any W-independent column compression.
**Why (term count, not hope):** the claim needs the slice's energy to lie in the next layer's dominant read directions; with a flat spectrum "dominant" is 51 % of M's energy at k = 128, and the slice is not even aligned to it (T1/T3 ≈ random). The consult's 72–78 % concentration is of the DELTA term in directions of the *tensor's* singular vectors (LENS_F:84), not of M_{l+1}; M's own singular vectors do not inherit it.
**Transport-cost answer (honest, n³ units/layer).** Even an exact read projection only helps the single next read. Per source-layer the chain pays ≈ 4 units: 2 dense transport products (P, A ← Φ∘Wᵀ·) + the read's 3 GEMMs partly shared (LENS_F 3 + 4r/n floor accounting). A basis V_{l+1} reduces the READ legs to n×k (projection ≈ 2·k/n = 0.25 units/source at k = 128 for P and A, then reads at ~k/n of full ≈ 0.4) but the CARRIED legs must stay full: V_{l+2} ≠ V_{l+1}, the Hadamard partners (A∘f2, X∘Y in read_block) do not commute with projection, so each layer needs the full n×n P, A (lift n²k per leg + the same 2 transport products), so transport remains 2 units/source-layer and total stays ≈ 2 + 0.25 + 0.4 ≈ 2.7–3.2 (best case, IF the projection were exact) vs 4 now, with truncation errors compounding over layers (each layer re-projects a different k-subspace; nothing recovers the discarded part). Moot here: the projection is 82–99 % wrong, so no saving exists to price.
**Prediction check:** KILL ✓; ADAPTED ≳ 30 % error ✓ (actually 82–99 %); RANDOM 80–95 % ✓ (98–99 %); ADAPTED ≈ W-INDEP ✗ (W-INDEP column compression is far better, 6–29 %; my row-frame control 34–47 %).
**G-RB82 KILL (W-adapted next-read basis; M_{l+1} spectrum flat, top-128 = 51 % energy; error 0.97 T3 / 0.99 T1 / 0.82–0.86 T2 vs bar 0.02; adapted ≈ random).**

Method. SE of the AB mean per element = |A-B|/2 (rms over neurons); chain error is DEBIASED with the cross product mean((c-A)(c-B)) (the independent noises kill the noise term), so error^2 is not inflated by noise. Report rms SE, debiased rms chain error, and SE/err per layer, pooled over nets (also relative to the rms of the quantity). (2) Split-half: rerun the four head-ON seat arms (var, k4, var_k3, var_k3_k4; layers 1-15, lam 1) with half=A and half=B on FIT 0,2,4,5,6,7 using the unchanged rb117 harness (copied into rb119, s117/w117 unmodified except the capture wrapper lives in a separate file); the four head-OFF arms too (secondary; ratios are vs the head-ON BASE as reported). Ratio = pooled sum of final MSE over the 6 nets / pooled BASE sum. Noise model: oracle MSE M(N) = M_inf + c/N (independent noise adds variance linearly to leading order), N_half = 2^22, N_full = 2^23, so M_inf = 2 M_full - M_half. r_inf = 2 r_full - r_half with r_half = mean(r_A, r_B) in pooled-sum terms (the BASE arm is noise-free so the ratio extrapolates linearly); also report 2 r_full - r_A and 2 r_full - r_B as the spread. A and B must agree (|r_A - r_B| small) or the 1/N model is not credible; if r_A and r_B differ by more than 0.03 the extrapolation is flagged unreliable.

A pair view needs an axis that splits a quadrant, i.e. a reshape (billed per element): get it for free by building the role's ONE arena view in the bit-split shape instead of the plain one.

The briefed bars are kept UNCHANGED; this note only fixes what the numbers can be compared with. Threshold mapping: p* = Phi(alpha): our twin p*=0.05 is alpha=-1.645 (MORE aggressive than his whole range), the shipped p*=0.02 is alpha=-2.05 (his most aggressive point, where matched/row = 0.9475).

FIT12 is in-sample for the frozen head, so only RELATIVE arm readings are used.
CHAIN FACTS the cuts must respect (s117 read): the prune zeroes cdf<p at the ageing step, so aged legs (P,A,T1,T2,Z,u,Q,Qb) AND the coincident term That (cdf^2 cdf) use the pruned gate, while the BIRTH keeps the unpruned f1,f2,f3 (A1=f1 Cz, T1=f1 B^T, T2=f2 U, c1..c4, u) -- the shipped mixed state. f2,f3,f1 are also the HUB-COLUMN coefficients in source_legs_z (Az*f2[None,:]), so masking f is a row AND hub cut. D = D21 = offdiag(Tz) -> rank-r (U,B); its residual Dadj = T_h - That -> Voff = 3 Dadj^T (D rows = Voff columns), d3 = diag(Dadj) is the diagonal level carried by the new source (s = d3 - ...).
OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS (one cold mask C = {cdf_unpruned < p} at the layer; every switch OFF by default in s131; mc_thr sets p):
 (ii) matched = shipped row prune at p PLUS: [mc_f] f1,f2,f3 *= ~C at birth (birth rows + hub coefficients; also u, T1, T2, c*); [mc_cols] A1[:, C] = 0 (birth hub columns of Cz); [mc_D] D21[C,:] = D21[:,C] = 0 before rank_r, and Dadj[C,:] = 0, d3[C] = 0 (D rows).
 (iii) = (ii) + saturated set S = {a = mu_z/sigma_z > 2.5} dropped: aged-leg rows of S zeroed in the same ageing mask (so That and u follow), D21[S,:] = 0 and Dadj[S,:] = 0 (off-diagonal D rows); the diagonal level d3[S] is KEPT. In this chain the level restore is native: Dadj = T_h - That, with That now lacking the dropped rows' coincident content, hands that diagonal content to the new source (s = d3 - ...). The chain has no carried kappa4 leg (k4z is the leg-independent SSC closure: it does NOT change when legs are dropped; asserted on 1 net). So (iii) is an ANALOGUE of E2, not a replication; variants: iii_nores (also d3[S]=0 = naive removal), iii_mv (+ explicit matvec diag(Tz) += (W^3)^T (k3_h o 1_S), the kappa3-level restore), iii_k4lit (+ literal matvec k4z += (W^4)^T (k4_h o 1_S), expected to double count).

**G-RB154 EXPLORATORY SCREEN (2026-10-21 ~05Z, orchestrator; NOT a gate, no build; writeup/proofs/k2_mix_screen.py): conditional-Gaussian mixture over input directions. KILL.**
- Idea: deterministic Gauss-Hermite quadrature over m input directions, X = V t + X⊥, with a K=2 chain per node (mean + full covariance; exact rectified-Gaussian diagonal; Mehler off-diagonal), then averaged. Cost m·2n³ per layer.
- Net 1340 (outside held-out 1300-1339; nothing fitted), final MSE:
  - plain K=2: 3.452e-6;
  - mix 1 direction × 8 nodes: 3.410e-6 (−1.2 %);
  - mix 2 × 4 = 16 nodes: 3.393e-6 (−1.7 %).
- Instrument check: Mehler order 12 vs 48 gives identical per-layer MSE, so truncation is not the cause.
- K=2 per-layer MSE is already 1.6e-7 at layer 2 and grows to 3.5e-6 at layer 16, about 170× our K=3 (≈2e-8).
- Reading: the non-Gaussianity that K=3 carries is born at EVERY layer (one ReLU makes z2 a sum of n non-Gaussian terms; κ3 is O(n^-1/2) per neuron and coherent across neurons). It is not carried by a few linear input directions, so conditioning on them cannot replace κ3. Kills the "quadrature over a common mode" family at K=2. For the write-up: a clean first-principles reason why κ3 is necessary, not merely helpful.
